pages.title: The Road Ahead
text: Jugcraft builds in stages, each needing parts from the ones before. Pick a stage on the left to see its steps.

pages.title: 1. Bronze Age
text: Get power running and double every ore.
Mine copper and tin and smelt bronze. Build a machine casing, a coal generator and copper cable.
Put the crusher first: every ore through it gives two raw ores, twice the ingots.
Bronze armor protects like iron; a Steampunk Pattern at a smithing table makes it Steampunk armor (see Steampunk and Kaiser Armor).

pages.title: 2. Workshop
text: Plates, wires and circuits: the parts every later machine needs.
Make plates in the metal press and wire in the wire drawer, then basic circuits.
Store power in a battery box. The pulverizer and ore washer take ore to three ingots each.
Find surface deposits with the prospector and put a deposit drill on them.

pages.title: 3. Rotation and Logistics
text: Move power by shaft and items by pipe and belt.
A steam engine or water wheel turns shafts; machines run on rotation directly, or a dynamo makes power.
Item pipes, extractors and conveyors carry ore from drills to furnaces without you.

pages.title: 4. Steel
text: Steel opens every heavy machine and the powered tools.
Bake coal into coke, then refine iron with coke into steel in the steel foundry.
The arc furnace melts what furnaces cannot. Advanced circuits need steel.
Charge a mining drill at the charging station.

pages.title: 5. Oil
text: Crude oil becomes fuel, plastic and asphalt.
Prospect for a reservoir and pump it with a pumpjack. Steel pipes and tanks carry the oil.
Distil it; burn diesel in a diesel generator. Crack heavy oil and reform naphtha in the cracker, make plastic, and run a gas turbine.

pages.title: 6. Chemistry
text: Salt, sulfur and air become acids, metals and gases.
Make brine and split it in the electrolytic cell into chlorine, hydrogen and lye.
The chemical reactor makes sulfuric acid, titanium sponge, lithium and rare earths.
Store a lot of power in a lithium battery bank. Split air for nitrogen and make ammonia and nitric acid.

pages.title: 7. Electronics
text: Silicon becomes chips and processors.
Pull silicon boules in the arc furnace, saw them into wafers and etch microchips in the lithography station.
Four microchips and an advanced circuit make a processor, for the top machines.

pages.title: 8. Late Game
text: Big, efficient power.
Magnet dynamos and motors lose almost nothing. Fit a turbocharger to the advanced engine and give it coolant water; a flywheel smooths out a bursty shaft line.
Solar trackers follow the sun; a field of heliostats around a tower boils water at a solar receiver. A flow battery stores 64 million JE.

pages.title: 9. Special Materials
text: Rubber, glass and weapons from the chemistry you already run.
Naphtha cracked to butadiene in the chemical reactor becomes rubber and gaskets, for sealed pipes and the turbocharger.
Borax turns sand into borosilicate glass: glass tanks that join into big see-through stores, tank gauges and optical fibre for processors. Guncotton fills grenades.

pages.title: Welcome, Engineer
text: This handbook covers every Jugcraft machine: what it does, what it needs and how to build it.
Pick a chapter on the left; it opens to show its pages. Scroll with the mouse wheel, or turn pages with the arrows or the arrow keys.
New here? The Progression chapter shows the order to build things in.
Power is measured in JE (Jugcraft Energy) per tick, fluids in mB (1,000 mB is a bucket).

pages.title: Your First Power
text: Mine tin and zinc, then make bronze (3 copper + 1 tin) by hand and smelt it.
Build a Machine Casing (bronze and zinc), a Coal Generator and some Copper Cable, then an Electric Furnace. Run cable from the generator to the furnace, or place them side by side.
Every machine holds its own charge, so it keeps working for a while after the power stops.

pages.title: Ores
text: Jugcraft ores appear in Overworld stone and deepslate. Regional exceptions are listed below:
Tin: Y -32 to 96, needs a stone pickaxe.
Zinc: Y -16 to 80, needs a stone pickaxe.
Lead: Y -48 to 64, needs a stone pickaxe.
Silver: Y -64 to 32, needs a iron pickaxe.
Nickel: Y -64 to 16, needs a iron pickaxe.
Tungsten: Y -64 to 0, needs a iron pickaxe.
Uranium: Y -64 to -16, needs a iron pickaxe.
Titanium: Y -64 to -8, needs a iron pickaxe.
Thallite: Y -32 to 48, needs a stone pickaxe. Richer in Lush Caves and the Glowcap Grotto.
Rock Salt: Y 0 to 64.
Phosphorite: Y -16 to 48.
Lepidolite: Y -48 to 32.
Monazite: Y -64 to 16.

Fluorite: Y -32 to 48. Large pockets below permanently snowy inland biomes; needs an iron pickaxe. Mineral faces in small stone outcrops can point to a pocket below. Seasonal snow, beaches, rivers and oceans do not qualify. The prospector and ore drill work here; nine fluorite make a decorative storage block. Fluorite chemistry is planned separately.

Spodumene: Y -16 to 64. Large pockets below Shield, Highland, Basin, Windswept Hills, Windswept Gravelly Hills, Windswept Forest and Stony Peaks; most centers are near Y 24. Needs an iron pickaxe. Look for pale-green mineral faces in small stone outcrops, or use the prospector and ore drill. The crusher gives two spodumene per ore; nine compact into a storage block. Fire spodumene in the Industrial Oven, then condition two activated spodumene with 500 mB sulfuric acid into two Lithium Carbonate. See Batteries and Power Management; existing lepidolite processing remains available.

Vanadium-bearing Iron: Y -48 to 32. Vanadiferous magnetite: richest below Shield and Volcano, with smaller, rarer pockets below Highland, Basin, Windswept Hills, Windswept Gravelly Hills, Windswept Forest and Stony Peaks. Centers peak near Y -8. Small stone outcrops sometimes mark pockets, except in Volcano. Needs an iron pickaxe; Fortune cannot increase the one raw feed per block. Crush one raw feed or intact ore into one Vanadium-bearing Iron Concentrate (200 ticks at 16 JE/t), then wash with 500 mB water into one Vanadium Oxide (200 ticks at 16 JE/t). Two bricks and the oxide make a reusable Vanadium Contact Bed, without acid. The prospector and ore drill work here; nine raw feeds compact into a storage block. Deposits never replenish. Ordinary iron shortcuts require the legacy configuration option.
Chromite: Y -32 to 64.
Cobaltite: Y -48 to 32.

Titanium-rich Mineral Sand: shallow beds in the Dune Beach, the Overgrown Beach and Beach. Look for surface streaks, then shovel the buried bed or use the prospector and powered Ore Drill. Each mineral-sand block is one finite feed unit; Fortune does not increase it. The Ore Drill leaves ordinary sand. Stockpile this feed for future separation/refining; the Deposit Drill and generic ore-doubling recipes do not process it.

Zircon-rich Mineral Sand: shallow beds in the Outback, the Lush Desert, the Dry River, Desert and Badlands. Look for surface streaks, then shovel the buried bed or use the prospector and powered Ore Drill. Each mineral-sand block is one finite feed unit; Fortune does not increase it. The Ore Drill leaves ordinary sand. Stockpile this feed for future separation/refining; the Deposit Drill and generic ore-doubling recipes do not process it.

Rare-earth-rich Mineral Sand: shallow beds in the Basin, the Lake District, the Lush River and River. Look for surface streaks, then shovel the buried bed or use the prospector and powered Ore Drill. Each mineral-sand block is one finite feed unit; Fortune does not increase it. The Ore Drill leaves ordinary sand. Stockpile this feed for future separation/refining; the Deposit Drill and generic ore-doubling recipes do not process it.

Garnet-rich Mineral Sand: shallow beds in the Gravel Beach, the Highland, the Shield, Stony Shore and Windswept Gravelly Hills. Look for surface streaks, then shovel the buried bed or use the prospector and powered Ore Drill. Each mineral-sand block is one finite feed unit; Fortune does not increase it. The Ore Drill leaves ordinary sand. Stockpile this feed for future separation/refining; the Deposit Drill and generic ore-doubling recipes do not process it.

pages.title: Geo-Resonance Prospector
text: Right-click to survey the 3x3 chunks around you, from the bottom of the world to a little above you. It shows which ores resonate, how strongly (1 to 5 bars) and roughly how deep, never exactly where.

pages.title: Deposit Drill
text: Three blocks square and two tall. Build it on a surface deposit (coal, iron, copper or tin, on stony hills): every 15 seconds it takes one coal or raw ore from each kind of deposit under it or one block round it, down to 3 blocks deep, using 16 JE/t. It pushes what it mines out of every side into a chest, item pipe, conveyor or machine beside it. Each deposit block holds 1,000 and then turns to stone; right-click one to see how much is left. Picks only break deposits, for nothing.
Uses 16 JE/t while working. Holds 20,000 JE.

pages.title: Ore Drill
text: Two blocks tall. Mines the ore blocks in a 9x9 column below it, one layer at a time down to the bottom of the world, one ore every 2 seconds. Each hole is refilled with stone or deepslate. The ores come out whole, ready for ore processing.
Uses 32 JE/t while working. Holds 20,000 JE.

pages.title: Ore Processing
text: Smelting an ore gives one ingot.
Crushing or pulverizing it first gives 2.
Washing it, then pulverizing the washed ore, gives 3.
Dissolving it in sulfuric acid in the chemical reactor gives 4 washed ores: 4 ingots.
Pulverizing ore sometimes gives a second metal's dust: copper gives gold, iron gives nickel, gold gives silver, tin gives tungsten, zinc gives lead, lead gives silver.

pages.title: Parts
text: Plates (Metal Press): copper, iron, tin, bronze, brass, invar, aluminum, nickel, lead, tungsten, steel, titanium, thallite, stainless_steel, aluminum_magnesium.
Gears (four plates): iron, bronze, brass, invar, steel.
Wires (Wire Drawer): copper, silver, aluminum.
Every part works with other mods' parts through c: tags.

pages.title: Coal Generator
text: Burns coal, charcoal, coal blocks or coke to make power. Coke lasts twice as long as coal, and charcoal three quarters as long. It stops burning when full, so fuel is never wasted.
Makes up to 32 JE/t. Holds 16,000 JE.

pages.title: Solar Panel
text: Makes power from daylight under open sky: 8 JE/t in sun, half in rain, nothing at night.
Makes up to 8 JE/t. Holds 4,000 JE.

pages.title: Steam Generator
text: Boils water with coal or bitumen: twice the power of the coal generator per fuel. A water source block directly below refills it for free.
Makes up to 64 JE/t. Holds 40,000 JE.

pages.title: Geothermal Generator
text: Two blocks wide. Burns lava from its tank (buckets, pumps or pipes): one bucket lasts 1,000 ticks.
Makes up to 64 JE/t. Holds 30,000 JE.

pages.title: Wind Turbine
text: Nine blocks tall with a seven-block rotor. The higher it stands and the worse the weather, the more it makes, up to 72 JE/t (twice that in a thunderstorm). The rotor needs a clear 7x7 square in front of the top.
Makes up to 72 JE/t. Holds 48,000 JE.

pages.title: Battery Box
text: Stores power. It charges from every side and gives power out of its front only.
Holds 400,000 JE; 256 JE/t in and out.

pages.title: Advanced Solar Panel
text: A white pedestal carrying a 3x3 array of solar cells on the layer above it: 64 JE/t in full sun (eight solar panels), half in rain, none at night. The cells need open sky. Cables meet the pedestal's foot.
Makes up to 64 JE/t. Holds 400,000 JE.

pages.title: Copper Cable
text: Carries power between generators, batteries and machines. It connects by itself to anything that stores or uses power on the touching face.

pages.title: Silver Cable
text: A faster cable: 1,024 JE/t, four times copper. Cable tiers join into one network, which carries as much as its slowest cable.

pages.title: Aluminum Cable
text: Steel-armored power line: 4,096 JE/t, for big batteries and the arc furnace.

pages.title: Steam Engine
text: Burns coal, charcoal, coke or bitumen and boils water to turn its flywheel: 64 KE/t out of its back. Right-click with fuel or a water bucket, or feed it with hoppers, pipes and pumps; a water source below refills it. It burns only while something takes the power.

pages.title: Large Steam Engine
text: Two by two by two. Four times the small steam engine: 256 KE/t out of a shaft at the back of its upper right block, using 40 mB of water per tick and fuel four times as fast. It has a screen like the steam generator's, and a water source under it refills it.
Needs no power.

pages.title: Hand Crank
text: Place it against a shaft, gearbox or machine and right-click: each crank turns it for 5 seconds (up to 20) at 16 KE/t. Cranking makes you a little hungry.

pages.title: Iron Shaft
text: Carries rotation (KE, kinetic energy) along its length, placed like a log. Machines at the end of a shaft line run straight off it: 1 KE counts as 1 JE, with no cables.

pages.title: Brass Gearbox
text: Passes rotation out of all six sides, to branch a shaft line or turn a corner. Power is shared evenly between everything on the line.

pages.title: Belt Pulley
text: A shaft with a grooved wheel. Use a Drive Belt on two pulleys with the same axis (level with each other along it, up to 16 blocks apart) and the second turns with the first: power jumps gaps and walls.

pages.title: Drive Belt
text: Links two belt pulleys: use it on one, then on the other. Breaking a pulley drops the belt.

pages.title: Dynamo
text: Turns rotation reaching any face into JE at 75% and pushes it into cables on every side: the bridge from a shaft line to the electric network.

pages.title: Electric Motor
text: Turns JE from cables back into rotation at 75%, up to 96 KE/t out of its shaft, which points the way you looked when placing it. Motor and dynamo together always lose power.

pages.title: Magnet Dynamo
text: A dynamo wound round rare-earth magnets: 512 KE/t into JE at 95%, against the copper dynamo's 128 at 75%. It pushes the JE into cables on every side.

pages.title: Magnet Motor
text: An electric motor with rare-earth magnets: takes 1,024 JE/t and turns it into up to 384 KE/t at 95%. Paired with a magnet dynamo it still loses a tenth every round.

pages.title: Flywheel
text: Stores rotation: a steel wheel that holds up to 2,000,000 KE. Shafts into any face but its front spin it up, 2,048 KE/t at most; its front shaft drives what it faces from the store at up to 2,048 KE/t. Friction takes a ten-thousandth of what it holds each tick, so it runs down when left alone. Right-click it to read how much it holds.

pages.title: Solar Tracker
text: A solar panel on a motorised mount that follows the sun from east to west: 20 JE/t all day in full sun (two and a half solar panels), half in rain, none at night. Cables take power from any side.

pages.title: Heliostat
text: A mirror on a post that follows the sun to keep its light on a solar receiver above it. It does nothing on its own.

pages.title: Solar Receiver
text: Put it on a tower over a field of heliostats: it counts those under open sky within 8 blocks across and 16 below, and makes 12 JE/t for each (up to 48, 576 JE/t) in daylight, boiling a mB of water for every 32 JE. Pipe water into it; cables take power from any side. Right-click it to read its field.

pages.title: Electric Furnace
text: Smelts anything a vanilla furnace can, twice as fast.
Uses 10 JE/t while working. Holds 10,000 JE.

pages.title: Crusher
text: Crushes one ore into two raw ores, minerals into extra minerals, cobblestone into gravel and gravel into sand.
Uses 16 JE/t while working. Holds 10,000 JE.

pages.title: Alloy Smelter
text: A 2x2 furnace that melts two ingredients together into alloys. Power goes in only through its copper socket, on the outer side of its lower right block.
Uses 20 JE/t while working. Holds 10,000 JE.

pages.title: Metal Press
text: Presses one ingot into one plate. Four plates craft a gear.
Uses 16 JE/t while working. Holds 10,000 JE.

pages.title: Wire Drawer
text: Draws one ingot into three wires.
Uses 12 JE/t while working. Holds 10,000 JE.

pages.title: Circuit Assembler
text: Assembles circuits from up to three ingredients, in any slots.
Uses 32 JE/t while working. Holds 20,000 JE.

pages.title: Arc Furnace Controller
text: The heart of the Arc Furnace: build a solid 3x3x3 cube of Arc Furnace Casing with this block in the middle of one face, facing out. It melts what an ordinary furnace cannot, and it pulls silicon boules: 4 silicon and a phosphate (the dopant) give a boule every 20 seconds. Pipe argon into the controller and it works twice as fast, for 1 mB a tick.
Uses 64 JE/t while working. Holds 50,000 JE.

pages.title: Auto-Crafter
text: Crafts the crafting recipe laid out in its 3x3 grid. Set the pattern by hand; each grid slot keeps its last item as the pattern, so it crafts while every filled slot holds two or more. Pipes and hoppers top up slots that already hold that item. Empty buckets and bottles go to the slot above the output.
Uses 8 JE/t while working. Holds 10,000 JE.

pages.title: Pulverizer
text: Grinds ore into two dusts, with a chance of a second metal. Also grinds washed ore, raw metal and ingots.
Uses 20 JE/t while working. Holds 10,000 JE.

pages.title: Ore Washer
text: Washes one ore into three washed ores, using 500 mB of water each time. Grind them in the pulverizer.
Uses 16 JE/t while working. Holds 10,000 JE.

pages.title: Sieve
text: Sifts gravel into flint and soul sand into soul soil, with a small chance of nuggets or quartz.
Uses 8 JE/t while working. Holds 10,000 JE.

pages.title: Sawmill
text: Cuts logs into six planks (four by hand) with sawdust, and planks into three sticks.
Uses 12 JE/t while working. Holds 10,000 JE.

pages.title: Coke Oven
text: Two blocks tall, needs no power. Bakes coal into coal coke, a hotter fuel and the carbon for steel.
Needs no power.

pages.title: Steel Foundry
text: Two by two and five tall, needs no power. Refines one iron ingot with one coke into one steel ingot. Pipe oxygen into it (from the air separation unit) and it blows the charge: twice as fast, for 2 mB of oxygen a tick.
Needs no power.

pages.title: Charging Station
text: Two blocks tall. Hang a drill, chainsaw or rocket pack on its cradle and it fills it from cables, 512 JE a tick; take it back with an empty hand. Its lamp lights while it charges.

pages.title: Mining Drill
text: Runs on JE instead of wearing out: 60 JE a block, 100,000 JE when full. Mines everything a pickaxe or shovel does, faster than netherite. Sneak and use it to switch mode: one block, a 3x3 square, or a whole ore vein. Empty, it mines like a bare hand.

pages.title: Chainsaw
text: A JE-powered axe that also cuts leaves: 40 JE a block. Cutting a log fells the whole tree above it; sneak to cut one log.

pages.title: Rocket Pack
text: Wear it and hold jump in the air to fly, 50 JE a tick (200,000 JE when full). Landing is safe while it fires. On a dedicated server, set allow-flight=true or long hovers get you kicked.

pages.title: Overclock Module
text: Mines 50% faster for twice the JE a block (up to 2). Fit it by using it on a charging station holding the tool; it is used up and stays in the tool.

pages.title: Range Module
text: The drill's area mode mines 5×5 (drill only). Fit it by using it on a charging station holding the tool; it is used up and stays in the tool.

pages.title: Capacity Module
text: Holds its base charge again (up to 2). Fit it by using it on a charging station holding the tool; it is used up and stays in the tool.

pages.title: Silk Touch Module
text: Blocks drop themselves (drill or chainsaw; not with fortune). Fit it by using it on a charging station holding the tool; it is used up and stays in the tool.

pages.title: Fortune Module
text: More ore drops, up to Fortune III (drill only; not with silk touch). Fit it by using it on a charging station holding the tool; it is used up and stays in the tool.

pages.title: Bronze and Steel Gear
text: Bronze and steel make swords, pickaxes, axes, shovels, hoes and armor, shaped like iron ones.
Bronze tools get the same drops as iron and last a little longer. Bronze armor matches iron's and is slightly tougher: knight's plate in copper-bronze, riveted in brass, with a brass collar.

Steel tools mine obsidian and ancient debris, and last over three times as long as iron. Steel armor sits between iron and diamond: knight's plate with a crested helm, layered pauldrons and a skirt of plates.
Steampunk and Kaiser armor keep the stylized looks bronze and steel armor were first made in, as sets of their own.

pages.title: Steampunk and Kaiser Armor
text: Steampunk armor is a bronze engineer's rig: an aviator cap with teal-glassed goggles, a breastplate with a pressure gauge, a copper boiler on the back, and buckled boots. Kaiser armor is the parade dress of the Winged Cog: a black spiked helmet with a gold plate, a field-grey tunic under a steel cuirass, gilt epaulettes and black jackboots.

At a smithing table, a Steampunk Pattern, a piece of bronze armor and a copper ingot make the Steampunk piece. A Kaiser Pattern, a piece of steel armor and a gold ingot make the Kaiser piece. Each pattern craft makes 4, one for each piece of a set. The Kaiser Pattern needs an Imperial Crest, made from black lacquer plates.

Same protection as the bronze or steel piece, in its own look: bronze and steel armor are knight's plate. Enchantments, wear, trims and plating carry over. The same pattern and an ingot of the metal turn it back.

pages.title: Kaiser Pattern
text: The Kaiser Pattern takes an Imperial Crest, the Winged Cog of the Kaiserworks blocks: three black lacquer plates, four gold nuggets, a gold ingot and a red dye make two crests.
Black lacquer plates come from iron plates and black dye.

pages.title: Thallite Gear
text: Thallite makes swords, pickaxes, axes, shovels, hoes and armor, shaped like iron ones. They mine and protect as iron does, wear out a little sooner, and take enchantments best of all.

Regrowth: thallite gear you wear or hold mends while you stand on living soil (grass, dirt, moss, mud or farmland): one use every 5 seconds, up to 75% of full. It never brings back a broken piece, so mending and anvils still matter.

pages.title: Earthbound Armor
text: At a smithing table, an Earthbinding Template, a piece of thallite armor and a gold ingot bind the piece into Earthbound armor, trimmed in gold, for good. It keeps its enchantments and wear.
Rooted: on natural ground (soil, stone, sand or gravel), each Earthbound piece takes 7.5% off knockback, 30% for a full set. With 2 or more worn, Regrowth works on stone, sand and gravel too.

pages.title: Arms: Swords
text: Bronze and steel make arms beyond the sword, each with its own way of fighting. All sweep like swords.
Longsword: a longer reach (3.25 blocks). Hold use to parry: it blocks 60% of a blow from in front, as a shield does all of it.
Greatsword: two-handed, slow and heavy, with a 3.75-block reach; a hit stops a shield blocking for 2 seconds.
Rapier: quick thrusts, two a second; its parry blocks 35%.

pages.title: Arms: Maces and Hammers
text: Flanged mace: a hit stops a shield blocking for 3 seconds.
War hammer: the heaviest blow of all, knocking foes back; a hit stops a shield blocking for 5 seconds, as an axe's does.
Both take Sharpness, Smite, Bane of Arthropods, Knockback, Looting and Fire Aspect.

pages.title: Arms: Polearms
text: Glaive: a blade on a pole that sweeps at 4.25 blocks.
Halberd: thrusts through every foe in line out to 4.5 blocks (not closer than 1); a hit stops a shield blocking for 3 seconds.
Spear: jab, or hold use to charge, as vanilla's spears do; faster on a horse or at a run.
Lance: a horseman's charge that hits harder and unhorses riders at lower speeds, reaching 5.5 blocks.

pages.title: Arms: Blades of Skill
text: Dagger: quick stabs at a 2.5-block reach; a blow from behind deals 50% more.
Sabre: quick sweeping cuts, and 3 more damage from the saddle.
Estoc: thrusts through mail, 0.3 more damage for each point of the foe's armor (at most 6).
Quarterstaff: two-handed, knocks foes back; hold use to parry 50% of a blow from in front.

pages.title: Arms: Heavy and Long
text: Battle axe: two-handed; chops wood like an axe and stops a shield blocking for 5 seconds.
Flail: a hit dazes the foe, slowing it for 2 seconds.
Scythe: wide sweeps at 4 blocks. Use it on a ripe crop to reap every ripe crop around it, 3 by 3, and replant them.
Pike: the longest reach, 5 blocks, but nothing nearer than 2; 50% more damage to riders and their mounts.

pages.title: Arms: Two Hands
text: Greatswords, war hammers, glaives, battle axes, scythes, quarterstaves, pikes and the two-handers swing with both hands: a click starts the swing, and the blow lands as it comes round, on every foe in its arc.
You slow to 40% of your speed while the swing is in the air. A click near its end follows straight on.
The last swing of each combo is the finishing blow, 25% stronger.
There is no hand left for a shield: with one in the off hand, a two-handed arm will not swing.

pages.title: Arms: The Two-Handers
text: Zweihander: the widest cleave, up to 5 foes; hold use to guard against 50% of a blow from in front.
Maul: the heaviest blow; its finishing blow shakes the ground, striking foes within 2.5 blocks and slowing them.
Executioner's sword: 50% more damage to a foe at or below 30% of its health.
Bill: a hooked polearm that pulls the foes it strikes towards you and drags riders from the saddle.

pages.title: Arms: Masterworks
text: Two-handed, set with a garnet (bronze) or a lit phosphor stone (steel):
Labrys: a double-bitted axe whose finishing blow whirls right round, striking up to 6 foes about you.
Battleblade: a saw-backed cleaver; each hit wears every piece of the foe's armor by 4 more.
War fork: a barbed fork set against a charge: 50% more damage to a foe coming at you.

pages.title: Arms: Kama and War Pick
text: Kama: quick hooking cuts. Use it on grass, ferns, vines or leaves to cut all of them about it, 3 by 3 by 3, dropping what they drop.
War pick: a beaked pick that fights and mines stone and ore as its metal's pickaxe does.

pages.title: Arms: Weapon Arts
text: Six arms each have a weapon art: a special move of their own, used with the use key. Each plays its own move and strikes in its own way; then the arm needs a few seconds before its art is ready again (shown on the hotbar). Plain blows are not held back.
An art's hits are the arm's own damage times a share, with its enchantments, and land in full even in quick succession. While busy with one you cannot swing.
Against one foe an art does no better than plain blows: it pays against many, or to get somewhere.

pages.title: Arms: Twinblade, Nodachi, Earthbreaker
text: Two-handed, all three.
Twinblade, Cyclone: 3 spins, each cutting every foe within 3 blocks all round and drawing them in.
Nodachi, Iaido: a dash of about 6 blocks; every foe you pass is cut a moment later, all at once.
Earthbreaker, Leap Slam: leap from the ground and slam where you land: hardest at the centre, and 15% more for each block you came down below your take-off.

pages.title: Arms: Katar, Moonblade, Kusarigama
text: Katar, Flurry: 5 quick jabs at the foe ahead, then a driving finish.
Moonblade (two-handed), Crescent: a wave that runs ahead about 12 blocks, through every foe in its way, weakening as it goes, until a wall stops it.
Kusarigama, Chain Lash: the chain catches the first foe in line up to 9 blocks off, hauls it in and the sickle reaps it as it comes.

pages.title: Arms: Katana and Brazier Mace
text: Katana, Seven Cuts: 7 cuts in a breath, each across every foe ahead (up to 4), leaving arcs in the air: crimson from bronze, pale gold from steel.
Brazier mace: a burning brazier on a haft. A hit sets the foe alight for 4 seconds; use it on a campfire, a candle or the ground to light it, as flint and steel does. Coal in its recipe.

pages.title: Arms: Longbow and Arbalest
text: Longbow: slower to draw than a bow (1.3 s for a full draw), but its arrows fly faster and flatter, and hit harder for it.
Arbalest: a crossbow with a metal prod, loaded as a crossbow is; its bolts fly faster and hit harder.
Shot for shot they beat a bow and crossbow, but not a second for a second. Both take their vanilla counterparts' enchantments and shoot ordinary arrows and (the arbalest) fireworks.

pages.title: Arms: Shields
text: Heater shield: a light shield of planks and metal, quicker to raise than a shield.

Tower shield: a great board that covers 130 degrees either side of ahead (a shield: 90), wears less for each blow it stops and braces you against being knocked back, but is slower to raise and slows you by 8% while held.
Hold use to block with either, as with a shield. An axe's blow still knocks them down for a while.

pages.title: Arms: Thrown Arms
text: A javelin, francisca, chakram or harpoon fights in the hand like any arm. Hold use to wind it back and let go to throw it, as a trident is thrown; a steel javelin's throw hits for 8, more with Sharpness and the like. It comes down where it struck, as itself, to be picked up again.
Javelin: flies far and straight. Francisca: tumbles end over end and knocks a raised shield down for 3 seconds.
Chakram: flies flat, cuts every foe on its way out (up to 12 blocks) and back, and returns to your hand. Harpoon: keeps its speed underwater and hauls what it strikes towards you.

pages.title: Arms: Styles
text: Four styles restyle a steel arm at a smithing table: gilded, ironclad, bonecarved, runebound. Put the style's pattern, the steel arm and the style's material in; the arm keeps its enchantments and wear.
Gilded (a gold ingot): longsword, rapier, sabre, halberd. Takes enchantments as gold does.
Ironclad (a steel plate): zweihander, maul, war pick, battle axe. Painted, plated and bolted; lasts twice as long.
Bonecarved (a bone block): dagger, flail, glaive, labrys. 20% harder against the undead.
Runebound (ectoplasm): nodachi, moonblade, staff, war hammer. Its runes glow, and a foe it strikes glows for 4 seconds, seen through walls.
Each fights as its kind does: the same swing, reach, trait and art.

pages.title: Arms: Trophies
text: Great foes carry arms of their own, with a boon.
These are met in their lairs. Anyone who takes part in one's fall may win its trophy, and always does the first time:
The Yeti King, in the Glacier Hall: Glacier Maul and Rimeclaw.
The Cinder Tyrant, in the Cinder Kiln: Cinderbrand and Magmaw.
The Mire Hag, in the Lantern Fen: Hagthorn and Bogfang.
The Crypt Lich, in the Archive of Last Names: Soulreaver and Gravewarden.
The Iron Dreadnought, in the Foundry Trench: Dynamo Halberd and Piston Hammer.
Vesperine, the Last Reaper, in the Hollow Acre: Vesper Scythe.
Madame Tatterlace, in the Spindle Loft: Needle Rapier.
These are yet to be met in the world, and will each carry two:
The Alpha Werewolf: Moonfang and Howler.
The Storm Roc: Stormcaller and Galefeather.
The Abyssal Leviathan: Tidebreaker and Leviathan's Hook.
Trophies last twice as long as steel, and fight as their kinds do.

pages.title: Arms: Armor Sets
text: Some armor sets have an arm of their own, made in the set's look, with a boon, and some a shield:
Hades Armor: Hades Scythe (Wither).
Sentinel: Sentinel Longsword (Mark) and Sentinel Shield (a shield).
Frost Knight: Frost Knight Greatsword (Frost).
Wight King: Wight King Zweihander (Drain).
Reaper: Reaper Scythe (Wither).

How they are won is still to be settled; until then they are found only in creative. They last twice as long as steel, and fight as their kinds do; a set's shield blocks as a steel heater shield does.

pages.title: Paxels
text: A paxel is a pickaxe, an axe and a shovel in one tool: it mines stone, wood and dirt at full speed.
Craft one from a pickaxe, an axe and a shovel of the same tier, from wood to netherite, bronze or steel. It lasts as long as all three together.

pages.title: Scuba Gear
text: Wear the scuba mask and the scuba tank together to breathe under water.
The tank holds 8,000 mB of oxygen. Use it on anything holding oxygen to fill it: a gas holder, or the oxygen tank of an electrolytic cell or air separation unit.
Under water it keeps your air full for 1 mB a tick: a full tank lasts 400 seconds of breathing.

pages.title: Free Runners
text: Rubber-soled boots that take away all fall damage and step up a full block without jumping.
They protect like iron boots and are mended with rubber.

pages.title: Power Katana and Power Bow
text: Two weapons that run on JE instead of wearing out. Charge them at a charging station; capacity modules fit both.
The power katana hits harder and faster than a netherite sword, for 1,000 JE a hit. Empty, it hits for 1.
The power bow fires arrows of energy for 500 JE a shot: no arrows needed, and they fly faster and hit harder. Empty, it is an ordinary bow that shoots your arrows.

pages.title: Powered Exosuit
text: Four pieces of armor as strong as netherite that run on JE. Each piece holds 400,000 JE and charges at a charging station; capacity modules fit.

Helmet: night vision whenever it is dark. Chestplate: an energy shield that regrows up to four hearts of absorption, and a jetpack (hold jump in the air). Leggings: 30% more speed. Boots: no fall damage and a full-block step.
Each piece works only while it is charged; a flat piece is plain armor.

pages.title: Liveries
text: The exosuit comes in Vanguard gunmetal. A Ronin livery at a smithing table, with a piece and red dye, repaints it crimson and silver, with the Ronin's hat and skirt; the power katana becomes the crimson Ronin katana.
A Vanguard livery with cyan dye paints it back. Repainting keeps the charge, modules and enchantments.

pages.title: Pneumatic Grapple
text: A harpoon gun on compressed nitrogen. It holds 4,000 mB; fill it by using it on the air separation unit's nitrogen or a gas holder. Each shot uses 25 mB.

The hook flies up to 32 blocks on its line. In a block, it reels you in fast with no fall damage and lets go with a hop at the end, so you can climb cliffs and cross gaps. In a mob, it drags the mob to you; bosses and golems are too heavy.
Use it again to let go. Party members are never hooked; other players only where PvP is on.

pages.title: Chemical Grenades
text: Thrown by hand or fired from the grenade launcher like the frag grenade. None of them breaks or burns a block.
Chlorine: a 3-block cloud for 10 s that hurts whatever breathes inside, through armor (not fish or the undead). Steel plate and nugget with 500 mB of chlorine in the chemical reactor.
Smoke: a 4-block screen for 15 s. Mobs lose sight of anyone inside; players inside without a mask can't see. Steel plate and sugar with ammonia in the reactor.
Thermite: a white-hot pool for 6 s that burns whatever stands in it, through armor. Thermite is an aluminum ingot and two iron dust; fill grenades like frag grenades.
Flashbang: blinds players who see it and staggers mobs (they lose their target, slowed and weakened). No damage.

pages.title: Gas Mask
text: Keeps out chlorine and smoke; its tinted lenses keep out a flashbang.
The filter wears a point a second in gas or smoke (220 s in all): repair it with charcoal on an anvil.
The scuba mask and tank also keep gas out while the tank has oxygen (20 mB a second).

pages.title: Foam Sprayer
text: Aim at a block up to 16 blocks away: foam fills the open space in front of it, up to 12 blocks at a time, through air, water, lava and plants. It never replaces a solid block or fills a space a mob stands in.
Bridge gaps, seal caves, stop a flood or a lava flow. Each canister holds 32 blocks of foam; make canisters in the chemical reactor from plastic pellets and an iron nugget in ammonia.
Foam breaks in a moment and drops nothing. Use cement on it to set it into concrete.

pages.title: Concrete
text: Cement mix: calcite (or a bone block), clay and sand; smelt it into cement.
Four cement, four gravel and a water bucket make eight concrete, as hard as stone and tougher.
Eight concrete round a rebar make eight blast-proof concrete: as blast-proof as obsidian, mined with a diamond or steel pickaxe. Both come as slabs and stairs.

pages.title: Medicines
text: Made in the chemical reactor. First aid kit: two cotton and a soap in bioethanol. Heals four hearts, then a 10 s wait.
Antidote: two charcoal and a bottle in lye. Clears poison, wither and every other harmful effect, and keeps the good ones (milk clears both).
Stimulant: four cocoa beans and a bottle in bioethanol. Speed II and Haste II for 60 s, with hunger.

pages.title: Bronze Fluid Pipe
text: Carries fluid that a pump pushes into it to every tank and fluid machine it touches.

pages.title: Steel Fluid Pipe
text: Like the bronze pipe, but carries 1,000 mB a tick for refinery flows. A pipe line carries as much as its slowest pipe, so one bronze pipe holds a steel line back to 250 mB.

pages.title: Fluid Valve
text: A steel pipe segment with a valve. Open, it carries fluid like a steel pipe; a redstone signal closes it, and the pipes on either side become separate lines. Its lamp is green while open and amber while closed.

pages.title: Fluid Filter
text: A steel pipe segment with a strainer. Fluid passes along it, but the tanks and machines it touches only get its chosen fluid (nothing until one is chosen). Use a filled bucket on it, or right-click it beside a tank holding the fluid (the way to choose a gas); sneak and right-click to clear it.

pages.title: Tinplate Tank
text: Holds 16 buckets of one fluid. Fill or empty it with buckets; right-click with an empty hand to read it.

pages.title: Electric Pump
text: Pulls water or lava from the block below it and pushes it out of its top and sides.

pages.title: Heavy Pump
text: A steel-tier pump: 1,000 mB a tick from below (water, lava or a tank) out of its top and sides, at 40 JE a tick, with a 16-bucket buffer.

pages.title: Joined Tanks and Gauges
text: Tinplate and glass tanks touching face to face join into one tank of one fluid, up to 64 of them. They fill from the bottom and drain from the top; pipes, buckets and comparators see the whole group.
A glass tank (four borosilicate glass in a steel frame) shows the fluid inside it.
Hang a tank gauge on the side of any tank or machine: its sight glass shows how full it is in eighths. Right-click it to read the fluid and amount; a comparator reads it too.

pages.title: Crude Oil
text: Crude oil lies in hidden reservoirs under some Overworld chunks. The prospector reports Oil (pumpable) and Shale oil (needs fracking) under the 3x3 chunks around you.
It is a thick, slow fluid that never makes new sources, so every reservoir runs dry in the end.
Pipes, pumps and tanks carry it like water; refineries turn it into fuels.

pages.title: Pumpjack
text: One block wide, three tall and three long; place it with the wellhead where you want the well. If the chunk under the wellhead holds pumpable oil (the prospector's Oil reading), it pumps 2 mB of crude oil a tick into its 16-bucket tank and pushes it into pipes and tanks touching it. A reservoir runs dry for good after 50 to 250 buckets; shale oil needs a fracking rig instead.
Uses 32 JE/t while working. Holds 20,000 JE.

pages.title: Distillation Tower
text: Two by two and seven blocks tall. Heats crude oil and splits each bucket into 100 mB of refinery gas, 250 mB of naphtha, 400 mB of diesel and 250 mB of heavy fuel oil, a bucket every 5 seconds. Each fraction comes out at its own height: heavy fuel oil at the base, diesel two blocks up, naphtha four up, and refinery gas at the top. Give each its own pipe or tank. Pipe heavy fuel oil in instead and it boils it under vacuum: each bucket gives 400 mB of lubricant (one block up) and two asphalt binder (in its slot), every 6 seconds.
Uses 128 JE/t while working. Holds 40,000 JE.

pages.title: Catalytic Cracker
text: Two by two and four blocks tall. Cracks heavy fuel oil into lighter fuels with steam and a catalyst: 1,000 mB of heavy fuel oil, 250 mB of water and a cracking catalyst give 500 mB of diesel (out at the base), 300 mB of naphtha (two blocks up) and 200 mB of refinery gas (at the top), every 8 seconds. Pipe naphtha in instead and it reforms it over the same catalyst: each bucket and a catalyst give 900 mB of gasoline (one block up) and 100 mB of refinery gas (at the top), every 6 seconds.
Uses 160 JE/t while working. Holds 40,000 JE.

pages.title: Fracking Rig
text: Three by three and five blocks tall. Place it with its front left block over shale oil (the prospector's Shale oil reading). Each powered tick it pumps 4 mB of fracking fluid down the well and brings up 6 mB of crude oil (out at the base), 2 mB of refinery gas (out at the top) and 3 mB of flowback water (out one block up), until the shale is spent.
Uses 256 JE/t while working. Holds 80,000 JE.

pages.title: Settling Plant
text: Three wide, one tall and two deep: settling basins and a filter press. It separates what settles. Flowback water from a fracking rig: each bucket gives 750 mB of clean water and a salt (a quarter is lost each time round). Oil sand (mined with silk touch) and 250 mB of water give 500 mB of crude oil and a block of sand; a bitumen and 100 mB of water give 150 mB. A block of mud gives four clay balls and 250 mB of water.
Uses 48 JE/t while working. Holds 20,000 JE.

pages.title: Fuel Values
text: What a bucket is worth: diesel 256,000 JE (diesel generator) or KE (diesel engine); heavy fuel oil 128,000; gasoline 384,000 and refinery gas 192,000 (gas turbine). Bioethanol from crops: 192,000 in the gas turbine, 256,000 KE in the advanced engine.
Refined all the way, a bucket of crude oil gives about 525 mB of diesel, 293 mB of gasoline and 183 mB of gas: about 282,000 JE, for about 40,000 JE of pumping and refining.
Oil never comes back: every reservoir runs dry.

pages.title: Diesel Generator
text: Three wide, two tall and two deep. Burns diesel or heavy fuel oil piped into its 8-bucket tank: 256 JE/t, a bucket of diesel every 1,000 ticks (256,000 JE) or heavy fuel oil twice as fast (128,000 JE a bucket). It refuses crude oil and other fluids.
Makes up to 256 JE/t. Holds 60,000 JE.

pages.title: Gas Turbine
text: Four wide, two tall and two deep. Burns gasoline or refinery gas from its 16-bucket tank: 512 JE/t, 384,000 JE a bucket of gasoline or 192,000 JE a bucket of gas. Its second tank takes lubricant from the distillation tower: 1 mB every second of running, and it stops when it runs dry.
Makes up to 512 JE/t. Holds 120,000 JE.

pages.title: Polymerization Reactor
text: Two by two and three blocks tall. Polymerizes refinery gas into plastic: a bucket of gas gives four plastic pellets, every 5 seconds. The metal press flattens each pellet into a plastic sheet.
Uses 96 JE/t while working. Holds 30,000 JE.

pages.title: Diesel Engine
text: Two wide, two tall and three long. Burns diesel (256 KE a mB) or heavy fuel oil (128) piped into its 8-bucket tank and turns a shaft out of the back of its upper right back block: up to 512 KE/t, twice the large steam engine. It burns only for the rotation the line takes.
Needs no power.

pages.title: Advanced Combustion Engine
text: Two blocks long, four cylinders. Burns gasoline (448 KE a mB) or diesel (320) piped into its 8-bucket tank and turns a shaft out of the back of its right-hand block at up to 1,024 KE/t, burning only for what the line takes. Through a magnet dynamo it is the best use of either fuel. Put a turbocharger in its slot and pipe water into its second tank: up to 1,536 KE/t, 10% more from each mB of fuel, using 2 mB of water a tick.
Needs no power.

pages.title: Hydrotreater
text: Two by two and three tall, its catalyst built in. Pipe diesel into its first tank and hydrogen into its second: 1,000 mB of diesel and 100 mB of hydrogen become 1,000 mB of premium diesel (base) and 100 mB of hydrogen sulfide (top), every 6 seconds. Or blend 900 mB of gasoline with 100 mB of bioethanol into a bucket of premium gasoline. 128 JE/t.
Uses 128 JE/t while working. Holds 40,000 JE.

pages.title: Premium Fuels
text: Premium diesel burns a quarter better: 320,000 JE a bucket in the diesel generator, 320,000 KE in the diesel engine and 400,000 KE in the advanced engine.
Premium gasoline: 448,000 JE a bucket in the gas turbine (gasoline and bioethanol apart give 364,800) and 512,000 KE in the advanced engine.
Hydrotreating pays best with the electrolytic cell's spare hydrogen. Its hydrogen sulfide goes to the chemical reactor: 200 mB make a sulfur dust, so oil becomes a source of sulfur for the acids.

pages.title: Heat Recovery Unit
text: One block, two tall. Put it against a running diesel generator or gas turbine: it boils water in their exhaust and makes 30% of their power again (77 or 154 JE/t). It needs water (1 mB per 64 JE, piped in or from a water source right below it) and lubricant (1 mB every 2 seconds). Two units on one generator share its heat.
Makes 30% of a touching generator's output. Holds 20,000 JE.

pages.title: Asphalt
text: Eight gravel around an asphalt binder (heavy fuel oil boiled in the distillation tower) make eight asphalt.
Walking on asphalt, its slabs or road line is 1.3 times as fast. Three asphalt make six slabs.
Four asphalt and a yellow dye make four road line blocks; the dashed line points the way you face when you place it.

pages.title: Cracking Catalyst
text: Bauxite (alumina) and sand (silica) with a nickel ingot make four. The catalytic cracker uses one for each bucket of heavy fuel oil it cracks or naphtha it reforms.

pages.title: Industrial Chemistry
text: Salt, sulfur, phosphate and bauxite get their real uses here.
Dissolve salt in water to make brine (chemical reactor), then split it in the electrolytic cell into chlorine, hydrogen and lye. Gases live only in tanks, pipes and gas cylinders.

pages.title: Electrolytic Cell
text: Three wide, three tall and two deep. Splits brine with electricity: a bucket gives 250 mB of chlorine (out of the top row), 250 mB of hydrogen (the middle row) and 500 mB of lye (the bottom row), every 20 seconds at 256 JE/t. Make brine in the chemical reactor from two salt and a bucket of water. It also splits plain water, slowly: a bucket gives 500 mB of hydrogen (middle row) and 250 mB of oxygen (top row) every 40 seconds, an early fuel for the fuel cell.
Uses 256 JE/t while working. Holds 60,000 JE.

pages.title: Electrolytic Separator
text: Two wide, two deep and three tall: the first of the big industrial machines, built from steel, copper cable and a basic circuit, before the Electrolytic Cell's aluminum cable and advanced circuit. It is placed from the front; every block it fills must be free, or it says what is in the way and where.

Pipe water or brine into the inlet low at the back. A bucket of water gives 500 mB of hydrogen (the top left collar) and 250 mB of oxygen (top right) in 40 seconds; a bucket of brine gives 250 mB of hydrogen, 250 mB of chlorine (top right) and 500 mB of lye (the return on the right) in 20 seconds. It draws 256 JE/t through the socket at the foot of the right tower.
It keeps its lye: when the lye tank is full, brine stops until the lye is piped away. Its screen says what it is waiting for, and upgrade cards fit its terminal.

Also makes peroxide from Oxygenated Process Water: the first outlet carries peroxide, the second returned water, and the third remains unused. Empty old products before changing jobs; see Advanced Electronics and Automation.

pages.title: Chemical Reactor
text: Two by two by two, lined with lead against the acid: the general chemistry vessel, with two item slots, liquid and gas feeds, a retained acid charge and a product tank. Two sulfur dust and a bucket of water make a bucket of sulfuric acid. It also mixes: two salt and a bucket of water make brine; two sand, a dried kelp and a bucket of water make fracking fluid. An ore in 250 mB of sulfuric acid gives four washed ores, the best ore route. Eight crops (wheat, sugar cane, potatoes, carrots, beetroot, berries, melon or apples) in a bucket of water ferment into 250 mB of bioethanol. Its other reactions are on its recipe pages. Absorption: 500 mB water + 500 mB hydrogen chloride gas makes 1000 mB hydrochloric acid; 250 mB water + 250 mB sulfur trioxide makes 500 mB sulfuric acid. Both take 5 seconds at 96 JE/t. For sulfuric absorption, first use a sulfuric-acid bucket on the TOP: the dedicated 1000 mB charge is retained, including in the dropped reactor. Normal liquid/gas feeds and products connect at the sides. Other process liquids are not preserved when broken: drain them first. HCl leaches one raw copper into two washed copper in 8 seconds. These are game recipes, not real chemical procedures.
Uses 96 JE/t while working. Holds 30,000 JE.

pages.title: Chemical Oxidizer
text: Two wide, two deep and three tall: a lined reaction throat fed by a hopper and a feed screw at the back, with a gas column and collector hood on top, built from steel plates, a furnace, an electric motor, glass, a basic circuit and a Machine Casing. Every block it fills must be free when it is placed.

Drop sulfur dust into the hopper on top at the back and pipe oxygen into the capped inlet low on the right. Each dust burns with 250 mB of oxygen into 250 mB of sulfur dioxide in five seconds, which leaves at the collar on top of the hood. It draws 96 JE/t through the socket low on the left side at the back.
Coal or charcoal burns the same way into 250 mB of carbon dioxide, the Chemical Infuser's feed for methane. Its screen says what it is waiting for, and upgrade cards fit its terminal.

Expanded processing is also available. Open Recipes to inspect each route's exact inputs, outputs and power, then lock a recipe for automation. Empty incompatible fluids before changing processes; old factory connections and recipes remain supported.

pages.title: Industrial Fermenter
text: Three wide, three deep and four tall: a tall stirred vessel on four legs, built from steel plates, a Steel Tank, glass, an electric motor, a basic circuit and a Machine Casing. Every block it fills must be free when it is placed.

Drop eight crops (wheat, sugar cane, potatoes, carrots, beetroot, berries, melon or apples) into the hatch on its crown and pipe water into the inlet low at the back left. With a bucket of water they ferment into 250 mB of bioethanol at the broth outlet low at the front, and 250 mB of carbon dioxide at the flange high at the back, in five seconds at 96 JE/t.
The carbon dioxide feeds the Chemical Infuser's methane. Collecting it is optional: when its tank is full the rest is vented and fermentation goes on.

Expanded processing is also available. Open Recipes to inspect each route's exact inputs, outputs and power, then lock a recipe for automation. Empty incompatible fluids before changing processes; old factory connections and recipes remain supported.

pages.title: Bulk Chemical Reactor
text: Four wide, four deep and four tall: the Chemical Reactor enlarged into a jacketed vessel with a stirring drive on its lid, built from a Chemical Reactor, a Steel Tank, a steel fluid pipe, an electric motor, a basic circuit and steel plates. Every block it fills must be free when it is placed. It runs two batches at once, from 8,000 mB tanks, at 90% of the reactor's draw.

Pipe water into the inlet on its left side and hydrogen chloride from the Chemical Infuser into the short absorption inlet on its lid: 500 mB of the gas dissolves in a bucket of water into a bucket of hydrochloric acid in five seconds, which leaves at the outlet low at the front.

Hydrochloric acid leaches ore like sulfuric acid: drop an ore into the hatch on its lid, pipe 250 mB of the acid into the side inlet, and four washed ores come out of the chute at the front, ready for the furnace.

Nitric acid in the side inlet and ammonia in the lid inlet neutralize each other: 250 mB of the acid and 125 mB of ammonia give four ammonium nitrate at the chute. It is a strong nitrogen fertilizer, and it packs grenades and high-explosive rockets in place of guncotton.
Also makes Wet Superphosphate from ground phosphate and phosphoric acid, or dissolves Mixed-farm Fertilizer into existing Nutrient Solution. Recipe lock selects the intended job.
Also prepares storable hydrazine and N2O4 propellants, each with a solid process residue. See Cryogenics and Rocket Fuels for compatible loaded motors and waste recovery.

pages.title: Anaerobic Digester
text: Six wide, six deep and six tall: a huge sealed tank on four foundation shoes, with a feed auger on its left side, a digestate chute low on its right, a gas header over its dome and a mixer gearbox at the back, built from four Steel Tanks, two electric motors, a steel plate, a basic circuit and a Machine Casing. Every block it fills must be free when it is placed. It runs four batches at once, from 16,000 mB tanks, at 80% of the reactor's draw.

Feed it organic waste at the auger: crops, rotten flesh, poisonous potatoes, kelp, pumpkins or seeds. Pipe water into the inlet low on the left. Sixteen items and a bucket of water digest over twenty seconds into 1,000 mB of raw biogas (60% methane, 40% carbon dioxide) at the header flange high on the right, and two bone meal at the chute.
Biogas upgrades into pure methane in the Chemical Infuser with its Nickel Catalyst Bed: 250 mB of biogas and 400 mB of hydrogen give 250 mB of methane and 400 mB of water.

Expanded processing is also available. Open Recipes to inspect each route's exact inputs, outputs and power, then lock a recipe for automation. Empty incompatible fluids before changing processes; old factory connections and recipes remain supported.

The expanded route collects liquid digestate at the lower rear-left outlet for the Filter Press. The original route still makes biogas and bone meal. This vessel retains four bulk lanes and 16,000 mB tanks.

pages.title: Coal Gasifier
text: Four wide, four deep and six tall: a tall lined reaction column over a broad ash chamber, with a charging chute on its left side and a gas header high on its right, built from steel plates, bricks, a furnace, a steel fluid pipe and a Machine Casing. Every block it fills must be free when it is placed. It runs two batches at once.

Drop coal or coal coke into the charging chute and pipe water into the inlet low on its left side. Each piece and 500 mB of water (as steam) become 500 mB of raw syngas (half carbon monoxide, half hydrogen) in ten seconds, which leaves at the header flange high on its right. Charcoal gives 400 mB from 400 mB of water.
Coal and coke each leave a Gasification Residue at the chute low on its right side. Bound with cement it makes concrete, and with asphalt binder road asphalt, in place of gravel.
Raw syngas is dirty: the Gas Cleanup and Separation Rack divides it into carbon monoxide and hydrogen.

Expanded processing is also available. Open Recipes to inspect each route's exact inputs, outputs and power, then lock a recipe for automation. Empty incompatible fluids before changing processes; old factory connections and recipes remain supported.

pages.title: Gas Cleanup and Separation Rack
text: Three wide, five deep and four tall: a scrubber column and two separation towers on a steel skid, built from steel plates, a Steel Tank, two Tinplate Tanks, an electric motor and a basic circuit. Every block it fills must be free when it is placed.

Pipe raw syngas into the inlet low on its left side. 500 mB of it is cleaned and divided into 250 mB of carbon monoxide (the tower at the back on the right) and 250 mB of hydrogen (the tower at the back on the left) in five seconds at 128 JE/t.
Carbon monoxide becomes methane in the Chemical Infuser with its Nickel Catalyst Bed: 100 mB of it and 300 mB of hydrogen give 100 mB of methane and 200 mB of water.

pages.title: Fuel Cell
text: One block. Combines hydrogen with the air: 128 JE/t, burning a millibucket of hydrogen a tick (128,000 JE a bucket). Pipe hydrogen from the electrolytic cell into it. Its screen lights while it runs.
Makes up to 128 JE/t. Holds 40,000 JE.

pages.title: Gas Burning Generator
text: Four wide, five deep and four tall: a gas engine turning a generator on a steel skid, built from steel plates, an electric motor, a steel gear, a Tinplate Tank and a basic circuit. Every block it fills must be free when it is placed; the corners above the skid at the front stay open.

Pipe hydrogen into the capped inlet low on its right side. It burns a millibucket a tick, 128 JE each, and sends 128 JE/t out of the socket on the terminal cabinet at the back: a bucket lasts 50 seconds. Its coupling and intake fan spin up as it starts.

Methane from the Infuser now burns here too: 448 JE per mB, up to 256 JE/t. Fractional fuel credit is saved, so switching loads or restarting loses and duplicates no fuel. This generator has no upgrade slots.

pages.title: Bio Generator
text: Three wide, four deep and three tall: a compact engine-generator on a thick skid, built from a Steel Tank, an electric motor, a steel gear, a basic circuit and a Machine Casing. Every block it fills must be free when it is placed.

Pipe bioethanol into the low liquid inlet on its right side. It burns 192 JE a millibucket at 96 JE/t, a bucket lasting 100 seconds, and sends the power out of the socket on the terminal box low on its left side. Its coupling and radiator fan turn while it runs.
It makes only as much as its store has room for. It also burns biogas from the Anaerobic Digester, piped into the same inlet: 268 JE a millibucket at 64 JE/t, a bucket lasting about 210 seconds.
Also burns cleaned biogas from the expanded scrubber chain at 268 JE/mB, up to 64 JE/t.

pages.title: Electroplating Bath
text: Plates a tool, weapon or piece of armor and repairs it fully, without experience, so enchanted gear keeps going. Put the item in the first slot and an ingot in the second, with sulfuric acid piped in: 10 seconds and 100 mB a plating. Nickel makes it half as durable again; silver gives a weapon Smite III; gold makes armor count as gold for piglins. Plate again with the same metal to repair; a different metal is refused.
Uses 32 JE/t while working. Holds 20,000 JE.

pages.title: Rubber
text: Crack a bucket of naphtha in the chemical reactor: 500 mB of butadiene. The polymerization reactor turns 500 mB of butadiene into four synthetic rubber.
Rubber and string make two belts. A steel plate faced with rubber cuts into four gaskets, and gasketed steel pipe comes four to a steel plate pair, without a bronze pipe.

pages.title: Glass Chemistry
text: Tincal, natural borax, crusts the sand of deserts and badlands; mine it for 1-3 borax.
Two sand and a borax melt into two borosilicate glass in the alloy smelter; the wire drawer pulls each into four optical fibre, which can carry a processor's signals instead of gold.
Iron and borax make ferroboron; a rare earth oxide with ferroboron gives two neodymium magnets, twice the old recipe.

pages.title: Plastic Blocks
text: Eight plastic sheets around a dye make eight plastic blocks of that colour, in all sixteen dye colours.
They are smooth, bright building blocks, as hard as concrete; mine them with a pickaxe.

pages.title: Chlorine and Lye
text: PVC: the synthesis converter joins 250 mB of refinery gas and 250 mB of chlorine into 250 mB of vinyl chloride; the polymerization reactor turns 500 mB of it into four PVC resin, and the metal press makes two plastic sheets from each.
Soap: boil two rotten flesh in 250 mB of lye in the chemical reactor for four bars. Use a bar to wash every status effect off, as milk does.

pages.title: Nitrogen Chemistry
text: Air is four parts nitrogen to one of oxygen. The air separation unit splits it; hydrogen comes from the electrolytic cell.
The synthesis converter joins hydrogen and nitrogen into ammonia, and burns ammonia in oxygen over water into nitric acid.
Ammonia and phosphate make fertilizer (six for two phosphate, against four with sulfuric acid). Nitric acid etches microchips with half as much acid as sulfuric.

pages.title: Air Separation Unit
text: Two by two and six tall: a cold box and its distillation column. It needs no input: it liquefies air and splits it, 8 mB of nitrogen a tick out of the top row, 2 mB of oxygen out of the bottom row and a little argon (1 mB every 2 ticks) out of the middle, at 64 JE/t. Pipe the gases to the synthesis converter, the steel foundry, the arc furnace or a gas holder; it stops while any tank is full.
Uses 64 JE/t while working. Holds 40,000 JE.

pages.title: Synthesis Converter
text: Three wide, four tall and two deep: a high-pressure catalytic converter. Haber-Bosch: 300 mB of hydrogen and 100 mB of nitrogen make 200 mB of ammonia. Ostwald: 100 mB of ammonia, 200 mB of oxygen and 100 mB of water make 200 mB of nitric acid. Each takes 2 seconds at 128 JE/t.
Uses 128 JE/t while working. Holds 60,000 JE.

pages.title: Chemical Infuser
text: Two wide, three deep and three tall: a stepped reaction chamber with an inlet on each shoulder, a catalyst-bed drawer at its foot and a cooling jacket behind, built from steel plates, two steel fluid pipes, a Tinplate Tank, copper cable and a basic circuit. Every block it fills must be free when it is placed.

Pipe hydrogen into the left inlet and chlorine into the right. 250 mB of each burn together into 500 mB of hydrogen chloride in under four seconds, which leaves at the top collar at the back. It draws 128 JE/t through the socket low on the right side at the back.

With a Nickel Catalyst Bed in its bed socket it makes methane: 400 mB of hydrogen and 100 mB of carbon dioxide (the right inlet) give 100 mB of methane at the top collar and 400 mB of water at the drain below it in ten seconds. The bed is never used up. Its screen says what it is waiting for, and upgrade cards fit its terminal.

Expanded processing is also available. Open Recipes to inspect each route's exact inputs, outputs and power, then lock a recipe for automation. Empty incompatible fluids before changing processes; old factory connections and recipes remain supported.

Install the reusable Cobalt-Ceramic Catalyst Bed for synthetic crude or CO/water gas balancing. First output carries crude or hydrogen; second carries water or CO2. Drain excess applies only to water. See Synthetic Fuels and Recovery.

pages.title: Ammonia Chiller
text: Ammonia boiling in its coils draws the heat out of water. Pipe ammonia into its first tank and water into its second: every 5 seconds a bucket of water freezes into a block of ice. Put four ice in its slot and it presses them into packed ice, and four packed ice into blue ice, against nine of each by crafting. Each batch loses 5 mB of ammonia. It works anywhere, even in the Nether.
Uses 24 JE/t while working. Holds 20,000 JE.

pages.title: Cryogenic Liquefier
text: A cold box of chrome heat exchangers under frost. Pipe oxygen (from the air separation unit) into its tank: every 4 seconds a bucket of oxygen condenses into 250 mB of liquid oxygen, the oxidizer for liquid rocket motors. 96 JE/t. Install a Methane Cooling Module for liquid methane, or an advanced Hydrogen Cooling Module for either methane or hydrogen. Tools are retained. See Cryogenics and Rocket Fuels for timings, storage and loaded motor assemblies.
Uses 96 JE/t while working. Holds 40,000 JE.

pages.title: Gas Cylinders
text: A gas cylinder carries 8 buckets of one gas: hydrogen to a far-off fuel cell, ammonia to a chiller, oxygen or nitrogen into the field.
Use it on a tank, gas holder, pipe or machine to fill it from there; sneak and use it to empty it back. Its bar shows how full it is.
Used in the air with a scuba tank or a pneumatic grapple in the other hand, it tops that up with oxygen or nitrogen.

pages.title: Grenades
text: Two cotton in 250 mB of nitric acid in the chemical reactor make two guncotton.
Two steel plates, a guncotton and an iron nugget make four grenades. Throw one with right-click; it goes off where it hits.
The blast hurts living things within 4 blocks, up to eight hearts at the centre, and walls shield from it. It never breaks a block.
The grenade launcher fires grenades from your inventory much further.

pages.title: Aluminum, the Real Way
text: Digest a bauxite in 250 mB of lye in the chemical reactor: two alumina.
Smelt two alumina with a coal coke anode in the electrolytic cell: two aluminum ingots, every 8 seconds.
That is two ingots from each bauxite, twice what the arc furnace gets and far more than the blast furnace's nugget.

pages.title: Titanium
text: No furnace can smelt titanium. Chlorinate it instead: a raw titanium, a coal coke and 250 mB of chlorine in the chemical reactor make a titanium sponge.
The arc furnace melts the sponge into a titanium ingot. Titanium frames the lithium battery bank.

pages.title: Leaching
text: Dissolve ores in sulfuric acid in the chemical reactor: a lepidolite and 250 mB of acid give two lithium carbonate, a monazite two rare earth oxide.
That is twice what the blast furnace gets.
Two lithium carbonate, four aluminum plates and a copper wire make two lithium cells.
The alloy smelter melts a rare earth oxide with an iron ingot into a neodymium magnet, for the magnet dynamo and magnet motor.

pages.title: Lithium Battery Bank
text: Three wide, two tall, one deep: six lithium battery modules holding 32,000,000 JE, eight capacitor banks. It charges from any side and gives power out of the sockets on its front, 16,384 JE/t.
Holds 32,000,000 JE; 16384 JE/t in and out.

pages.title: Flow Battery
text: Three wide, three tall, two deep: a vanadium redox flow battery. It holds 1,000 JE for every mB of vanadium electrolyte in its tank, so 64,000,000 JE with all 64 buckets in. Fill it by pipe or bucket; the electrolyte stays in it (also when broken). It charges from any side and gives power out of its front, 8,192 JE/t. Make the electrolyte in the chemical reactor from two asphalt binder and a bucket of sulfuric acid.
Holds 64,000,000 JE; 8192 JE/t in and out.

pages.title: Fertilizer
text: Two phosphate and 250 mB of sulfuric acid in the chemical reactor make four fertilizer.
Use one on the ground or a crop: every crop in the 5x5 area around it (a block up or down too) gets two doses of bone meal. Grass and saplings are left alone.

pages.title: Gas Scrubber
text: One Gas Scrubber cleans synthesis gas, raw biogas and wet fermentation CO2. Feed gas and wash water into their labeled inputs. Outlet 1 collects CO/clean biogas/CO2; outlet 2 collects hydrogen/wash digestate/water respectively. Capture solid synthesis-gas residue in the drawer.

Open Recipes to search and preview jobs. Lock recipe limits new batches; Automatic restores input-based selection. Locks persist across saves; current batches finish unchanged. Drain incompatible input AND output fluids and remove other feed items before changing jobs. Empty outputs for sustained automation. You can use one machine for different jobs or dedicate identical copies to separate factory lines.

Three wide, five deep and four tall. A stepped wash tower, collection pot, separator, closed pipe loops and service bridge share one machine. Dirty gas enters high at the rear; wash water enters low on the left. The two front upper outlets give carbon monoxide on the left, hydrogen on the right. Residue leaves the low front drawer.

500 mB dirty synthesis gas + 125 mB wash water gives 250 mB carbon monoxide, 250 mB hydrogen and one wet mixed residue in 100 ticks at 48 JE/t. Both gases and the residue must fit before work starts. There are no disposable filters.

Stabilize one residue with clay and two gravel into two cobblestone road-fill blocks. That consumes the residue once; it gives no second fuel or recovered metals. Existing gas cylinders, tanks and pipes carry every new gas. Feed the cleaned hydrogen and carbon monoxide to an Infuser; methane drives the Gas Burning Generator at 256 JE/t, 448 JE/mB.

pages.title: Biogas Cleaner
text: Optional specialist model: existing machines, recipes, inventories and production remain supported. For a new factory, build the Gas Scrubber, which also runs this machine's processes. This specialist stays craftable for existing layouts but is omitted from the main creative machinery list.

Two wide, three deep and three tall. The sealed wash tower and demister clean biogas without splitting its 60/40 composition. Raw gas enters upper rear right; wash water enters lower rear left. Cleaned gas leaves upper front right; dirty wash leaves lower front right. Power enters front left.

1000 mB raw biogas + 250 mB water -> 1000 mB cleaned biogas + 250 mB wash digestate, 100 ticks at 24 JE/t. Route that wash to the Digestate Separator with the digester residue. No disposable filter is needed. Full product tanks stop processing without wasting inputs.

Also cleans wet fermentation CO2: 250 mB gas + 250 mB wash water -> 250 mB usable CO2 + 250 mB recovered water, 100 ticks at 24 JE/t. Drain both previous products before switching between biogas and fermentation gas. No new disposable filter or separate gas-cleaning machine is needed.

pages.title: Digestate Separator
text: Optional specialist model: existing machines, recipes, inventories and production remain supported. For a new factory, build the Filter Press, which also runs this machine's processes. This specialist stays craftable for existing layouts but is omitted from the main creative machinery list.

Two wide, three deep and three tall. A closed screw press with guarded drive and collection drawer. Feed digestate at the rear left; recovered water leaves the rear right; fiber leaves the lower front right drawer. Power enters the front left.

1000 mB digestate -> 750 mB reusable water + one Digestate Fiber in 100 ticks at 16 JE/t. Eight fibers craft one existing Fertilizer, usable in the farming and hydroponics systems. Fertilizer and recovered water are never accepted as biomass feed, and water alone cannot produce fuel.

pages.title: Heated Mashing Station
text: Three wide, deep and tall. Mill and heat 16 fermentable crops with 1000 mB water into 1250 mB mash, 200 ticks at 24 JE/t. The grain hopper, guarded milling drive and insulated mash kettle share one machine. Existing crop and water producers supply it; water alone cannot make fuel.

Power: lower front left socket. Left/right descriptions use the view from the front. Rear: water low left, mash low middle. Solid inputs are front-right hatches and solid outputs rear-right hatches. Each pipe is physically routed into its vessel, pump or collection tray. Use existing pipes, tanks, cylinders, cables and conveyors; earlier steel/copper/ceramics supply all crafting bills.

pages.title: Chemical Distillation Station
text: Four wide/deep and six tall. Feed 1000 mB fermented broth; collect 500 mB existing Bioethanol and 500 mB Stillage, 200 ticks at 32 JE/t. A heated column, condenser, reboiler, pump and service ladder separate these products. Both outputs must fit.

Ethanol already fuels the Bio-Generator and existing compatible engines. The digester accepts 1000 mB stillage instead of solid farm feed, producing 250 mB raw biogas and 500 mB digestate in 300 ticks at 22 JE/t per expanded lane. Continue through the existing cleaner and separator. Pure water and digestate cannot make ethanol. Dehydration is reserved for a future real consumer; the original direct reactor ethanol recipe remains.

Power: lower front left socket. Left/right descriptions use the view from the front. Rear: broth midway up toward the right, ethanol midway up at the left, stillage low toward the right. Solid inputs are front-right hatches and solid outputs rear-right hatches. Each pipe is physically routed into its vessel, pump or collection tray. Use existing pipes, tanks, cylinders, cables and conveyors; earlier steel/copper/ceramics supply all crafting bills.

Also recovers water from Treated Process Water: first outlet water, second Process Recovery Concentrate. Use the existing recipe picker, output previews and Lock recipe to separate this from ethanol and titanium jobs.

Also vaporizes LOX, liquid methane or liquid hydrogen into the matching gas through the first outlet. Each paid batch expands 250 mB liquid to 1000 mB gas; clear old outputs and lock the desired recipe.

pages.title: Bauxite Digestion Vessel
text: Three wide, four deep and three tall. One existing Bauxite + 250 mB lye + 750 mB water -> 1000 mB aluminate slurry, 200 ticks at 64 JE/t. The sealed horizontal vessel has a locking cover, heat jacket, feed hatch and service pipes. Mine or trade bauxite and make lye with the copper-built Electrolytic Separator.

Power: lower front left socket. Left/right descriptions use the view from the front. Rear: lye midway up at the left, water midway up in the middle, slurry low right. Solid inputs are front-right hatches and solid outputs rear-right hatches. Each pipe is physically routed into its vessel, pump or collection tray. Use existing pipes, tanks, cylinders, cables and conveyors; earlier steel/copper/ceramics supply all crafting bills.

pages.title: Filter Press
text: One Filter Press handles aluminate slurry and digestate. Aluminate produces aluminum hydroxide, bauxite residue, lye at outlet 1 and water at outlet 2. Digestate produces fiber and water at outlet 1; its second liquid/solid outlets remain unused.

Open Recipes to search and preview jobs. Lock recipe limits new batches; Automatic restores input-based selection. Locks persist across saves; current batches finish unchanged. Drain incompatible input AND output fluids and remove other feed items before changing jobs. Empty outputs for sustained automation. You can use one machine for different jobs or dedicate identical copies to separate factory lines.

Three wide, four deep and three tall. 1000 mB slurry -> two Aluminum Hydroxide, one Bauxite Residue, 200 mB recovered lye and 500 mB water, 160 ticks at 32 JE/t. Return lye to digestion, adding 50 mB makeup per bauxite. Both liquid and both solid outputs must have room.

One residue + one clay ball + two gravel craft two cobblestone as stabilized game filler. Raw bauxite residue is not fertilizer or digester feed. The press uses visible filter plates, clamping rods, a collection trough and separate output drawers.

Power: lower front left socket. Left/right descriptions use the view from the front. Rear: slurry midway up in the middle, recovered lye low left and water low middle. Two solid output hatches sit on the right. Solid inputs are front-right hatches and solid outputs rear-right hatches. Each pipe is physically routed into its vessel, pump or collection tray. Use existing pipes, tanks, cylinders, cables and conveyors; earlier steel/copper/ceramics supply all crafting bills.
Also filters phosphate slurry: first fluid outlet phosphoric acid, second water, first solid output gypsum-rich residue. See Phosphate Processing and Fertilizers.

pages.title: Industrial Oven
text: One Industrial Oven calcines aluminum hydroxide, dries magnesium chloride solution and sinters PTFE blanks. A new lower-rear solution inlet feeds drying; the old solid hatches and condensate outlet stay in place. Solid recipes require the solution tank to be empty. All recipes retain their original costs and products.

Open Recipes to search and preview jobs. Lock recipe limits new batches; Automatic restores input-based selection. Locks persist across saves; current batches finish unchanged. Drain incompatible input AND output fluids and remove other feed items before changing jobs. Empty outputs for sustained automation. You can use one machine for different jobs or dedicate identical copies to separate factory lines.

Three wide, four deep and three tall. Two hydroxide -> two existing Alumina + 250 mB recovered water, 200 ticks at 64 JE/t. Reuse this water with the press water. Enclosed ceramic kiln, guarded drive, insulated service hood and front charge door; all heating is paid electricity. Alumina keeps its existing catalyst and metal consumers.

Power: lower front left socket. Left/right descriptions use the view from the front. Rear: recovered water midway up at the left, alumina in the right hatch. Solid inputs are front-right hatches and solid outputs rear-right hatches. Each pipe is physically routed into its vessel, pump or collection tray. Use existing pipes, tanks, cylinders, cables and conveyors; earlier steel/copper/ceramics supply all crafting bills.

Also fires porcelain, alumina and zirconia blanks and calcines zirconia precursor. The solution tank must be empty for dry firing. Use Recipes to select a ceramic job; old calcination, drying and PTFE recipes remain supported.
Also dries Wet Superphosphate, returning water, and prepares Washed Gypsum into the existing Gypsum Binder. Empty incompatible stored outputs before switching jobs.

pages.title: Aluminum Reduction Cell
text: Three wide/deep and four tall. Two Alumina + one Coke -> two existing Aluminum Ingots + 250 mB CO2, 400 ticks at 96 JE/t. Copper busbars and clay bricks start the line without requiring its own aluminum. Carbon is consumed once per batch; there is no electrode repair meter.

Default collect-and-vent excess CO2, or select Keep gas before starting. Ingots must always fit. Existing aluminum wire, cable, plates and structural/vehicle recipes remain the useful destinations. The larger molten-salt hall, alloy expansion and new specialized products are later work.

Power: lower front left socket. Left/right descriptions use the view from the front. Rear: CO2 midway up at the left, ingots in the right hatch. Front right: lower hatch takes alumina, upper hatch takes coke. Solid inputs are front-right hatches and solid outputs rear-right hatches. Each pipe is physically routed into its vessel, pump or collection tray. Use existing pipes, tanks, cylinders, cables and conveyors; earlier steel/copper/ceramics supply all crafting bills.

pages.title: Coastal Seawater Intake
text: Renewable coastal resource collection: 200 mB seawater for 320 JE per one-second stroke (average 10 mB and 16 JE/t). Place the lower front-right intake against open water at sea level (water surface block Y = sea level - 1) in the Overworld. It samples a 3 by 3 water patch extending forward from its mouth, two source-water blocks deep. Every column must be beach/ocean-tagged and open to the sky; the loaded surrounding region must contain ocean biome. No shoreline blocks are removed.

An inland pond, elevated bucket pool, flowing water, sodium-chloride brine or pipe-fed ordinary water cannot provide this mineral feed. Coastal restoration of a qualifying shore is allowed; vanilla does not record historical ownership of water blocks. No remote intake or chunk loading. Power and output space are required; pause stops collection.

Power socket: lower front-left. Solid feed hatches: front-right, bottom to top. Solid outputs: rear-right, bottom to top. Liquid inputs: rear middle height, left to right viewed from the front. Liquid outputs: rear bottom, left to right. Read JEI for exact materials. All tubes terminate at the parts they serve; machines share existing pipes, cables and automation. Game quantities are not real manufacturing instructions.

pages.title: Concentrator
text: One Concentrator handles coastal seawater and ordinary sulfuric acid. It replaces the need to build a separate Acid Concentrator. Product leaves outlet 1; recovered water leaves outlet 2. Each process keeps its original ingredients, yields, time and power.

Open Recipes to search and preview jobs. Lock recipe limits new batches; Automatic restores input-based selection. Locks persist across saves; current batches finish unchanged.
