Drain incompatible input AND output fluids and remove other feed items before changing jobs. Empty outputs for sustained automation. You can use one machine for different jobs or dedicate identical copies to separate factory lines.

1000 mB distinct coastal seawater -> 250 mB magnesium-bearing brine + 750 mB recovered water. 200 ticks at 32 JE/t. The short evaporator column, supported condenser and collection sump share one skid. Ordinary water and sodium-chloride brine are rejected.

Power socket: lower front-left. Solid feed hatches: front-right, bottom to top. Solid outputs: rear-right, bottom to top. Liquid inputs: rear middle height, left to right viewed from the front. Liquid outputs: rear bottom, left to right. Read JEI for exact materials. All tubes terminate at the parts they serve; machines share existing pipes, cables and automation. Game quantities are not real manufacturing instructions.

pages.title: Mineral Conditioning Station
text: 250 mB magnesium brine + 250 mB lye -> one magnesium hydroxide + 500 mB spent mineral wash; 160 ticks at 24 JE/t. Then change feeds: one hydroxide + 500 mB existing hydrochloric acid -> 500 mB prepared chloride solution and 250 mB water; 160 ticks at 32 JE/t.

Drain old tanks before switching recipes. Settle 500 mB spent wash into one existing salt and 250 mB water for 120 ticks at 16 JE/t; the rest is evaporation/loss in game accounting. The same station treats titanium-distillation wash. Neither wash nor ordinary salt brine supplies magnesium.

Power socket: lower front-left. Solid feed hatches: front-right, bottom to top. Solid outputs: rear-right, bottom to top. Liquid inputs: rear middle height, left to right viewed from the front. Liquid outputs: rear bottom, left to right. Read JEI for exact materials. All tubes terminate at the parts they serve; machines share existing pipes, cables and automation. Game quantities are not real manufacturing instructions.

Also prepares ceramic powder charges with water and recovers trace zircon from sand. See Ceramics and Precision in the Handbook for the whole route. Clear incompatible fluids and lock the desired job when switching.
Also washes regional chromite: two minerals and 250 mB water make two concentrate. The Arc Furnace reduces two concentrate with one Coke into two Ferrochromium Ingots for stainless alloying.
Also prepares organic fertilizer carriers from compost or digestate fibre, and washes gypsum-rich residue with water. The gypsum route requires room for Spent Mineral Wash.

Also prepares primary cobalt stock and treats wafer waste with calcite and lye. Treated water and recovery concentrate require separate outlets; concentrate can be stabilized with clay. No acid or solvent is recovered from the fungible mixture.

pages.title: Chloride Drying Oven
text: Optional specialist model: existing machines, recipes, inventories and production remain supported. For a new factory, build the Industrial Oven, which also runs this machine's processes. This specialist stays craftable for existing layouts but is omitted from the main creative machinery list.

500 mB prepared magnesium chloride solution -> one Dry Magnesium Chloride and 500 mB recovered condensate. 160 ticks at 48 JE/t includes paid conditioning/drying. Feed the dry item to the magnesium cell, never aqueous solution.

Power socket: lower front-left. Solid feed hatches: front-right, bottom to top. Solid outputs: rear-right, bottom to top. Liquid inputs: rear middle height, left to right viewed from the front. Liquid outputs: rear bottom, left to right. Read JEI for exact materials. All tubes terminate at the parts they serve; machines share existing pipes, cables and automation. Game quantities are not real manufacturing instructions.

pages.title: Magnesium Electrolysis Cell
text: One dry prepared MgCl2 -> one Magnesium Ingot + 250 mB chlorine; 400 ticks at 64 JE/t. Automatic internal heating is included in paid work. Capture all chlorine: a full outlet stops the batch. Steel, copper and clay build the first cell. Titanium recovery returns the same dry chloride, not extra metal; the same paid recipe handles both supplies.

Power socket: lower front-left. Solid feed hatches: front-right, bottom to top. Solid outputs: rear-right, bottom to top. Liquid inputs: rear middle height, left to right viewed from the front. Liquid outputs: rear bottom, left to right. Read JEI for exact materials. All tubes terminate at the parts they serve; machines share existing pipes, cables and automation. Game quantities are not real manufacturing instructions.

pages.title: Titanium Chlorination Vessel
text: One existing Raw Titanium + one Coke + 500 mB chlorine -> 1000 mB crude titanium chloride + 250 mB CO2. 240 ticks at 64 JE/t. Default captures CO2 that fits and vents excess; Keep gas stops for full storage. The crude product always needs room.

Existing Chemical Distillation Station: 1000 mB crude chloride -> 750 mB purified chloride + 250 mB spent mineral wash, 240 ticks at 48 JE/t. Empty ethanol/stillage before changing jobs. Process wash in the Mineral Conditioning Station.

Power socket: lower front-left. Solid feed hatches: front-right, bottom to top. Solid outputs: rear-right, bottom to top. Liquid inputs: rear middle height, left to right viewed from the front. Liquid outputs: rear bottom, left to right. Read JEI for exact materials. All tubes terminate at the parts they serve; machines share existing pipes, cables and automation. Game quantities are not real manufacturing instructions.

pages.title: Titanium Reduction Retort
text: 750 mB purified titanium chloride + two Magnesium Ingots -> one existing clean Titanium Sponge + two Dry Magnesium Chloride. 400 ticks at 96 JE/t includes internal separation and sponge cleanup. Both drawers must fit. Re-electrolyze both salt items to recover two Mg and 500 mB chlorine; it costs power, never generates it.

The existing Arc Furnace melts each sponge into one titanium ingot. Existing titanium tools, armor and components use it. Old titanium recipes remain available. First construction uses steel/copper/ceramics, never its own titanium or magnesium output.

Power socket: lower front-left. Solid feed hatches: front-right, bottom to top. Solid outputs: rear-right, bottom to top. Liquid inputs: rear middle height, left to right viewed from the front. Liquid outputs: rear bottom, left to right. Read JEI for exact materials. All tubes terminate at the parts they serve; machines share existing pipes, cables and automation. Game quantities are not real manufacturing instructions.

pages.title: Polymer Molding Press
text: Fit one reusable mold in the mold socket; it is locked during a batch and never consumed or worn. All six products take 120 ticks at 32 JE/t. Housings/panels accept existing plastic pellets, PVC resin or new HDPE pellets through an explicit rigid-polymer tag. Fittings require PVC. Insulation, gaskets and hoses require rubber.

Four rigid stock -> one housing or panel; two PVC -> two fittings; two rubber -> three insulation pieces or two existing gaskets; three rubber -> one hose. Housing assembles machine casings; fittings reinforce bronze pipes into steel pipes; insulation assembles copper cable; hoses assemble pipe valves; panels combine with coke into existing carbon-composite building/vehicle panels. These are additional routes, not new gates on old recipes.

Six distinct molds are made from earlier steel plates and simple pattern items. There is no free offcut award: all allocated feed becomes the listed parts. The Polymer Extruder and Clean Polymer Reclaimer add continuous shaping and same-grade offcut recovery. Named ethylene, HDPE, LDPE and staged PVC now connect through the Monomer Preparation Unit and Polymerization Kettle.

Power socket: lower front-left. Solid feed hatches: front-right, bottom to top. Solid outputs: rear-right, bottom to top. Liquid inputs: rear middle height, left to right viewed from the front. Liquid outputs: rear bottom, left to right. Read JEI for exact materials. All tubes terminate at the parts they serve; machines share existing pipes, cables and automation. Game quantities are not real manufacturing instructions.

pages.title: Monomer Preparation Unit
text: Refinery gas (1000 mB) yields 500 mB named ethylene. Renewable route: 1000 mB bioethanol yields 500 mB ethylene and 250 mB water, with paid dehydration. All process heat is included in JE use; no manual pressure controls.

500 mB ethylene + 500 mB chlorine -> 1000 mB ethylene dichloride; then 1000 mB dichloride -> 500 mB vinyl chloride and 500 mB hydrogen chloride gas. Absorb recovered HCl in the existing Chemical Reactor. Empty incompatible tank contents before switching jobs. Both outlets must fit; nothing is silently vented. Earlier PVC routes remain available.

Power: lower front-left. Solid feed: front-right. Finished product: rear-right middle; extrusion offcuts: rear-right upper. Fluid feed: rear middle; fluid products: rear bottom. Pause, Cancel, progress, tank levels, energy, tool locks and upgrade slots use the shared factory screen. Recipes are fictional game quantities.

pages.title: Polymerization Kettle
text: 1000 mB ethylene makes four HDPE or LDPE pellets according to the reusable insert in the protected socket. HDPE uses a catalyst cartridge; LDPE uses its process insert. These select distinct paid processing recipes; they are not consumed. PVC and rubber use existing vinyl chloride and butadiene respectively and need no insert.

HDPE substitutes for ordinary rigid stock in the existing Molding Press, making housings and vehicle panels. LDPE belongs to flexible film, not the rigid-stock tag. The kettle needs only earlier steel, copper and ceramics; HDPE tooling adds existing titanium/magnesium stock.

Power: lower front-left. Solid feed: front-right. Finished product: rear-right middle; extrusion offcuts: rear-right upper. Fluid feed: rear middle; fluid products: rear bottom. Pause, Cancel, progress, tank levels, energy, tool locks and upgrade slots use the shared factory screen. Recipes are fictional game quantities.

pages.title: Polymer Extruder
text: Continuous shaping on a supported heated barrel, cooling bed and draw rollers. Install a reusable sheet, film, profile, hose or insulation die. Feed HDPE or existing PVC for sheets, LDPE for film, PVC for profiles, or rubber for hoses/insulation. Tool sockets lock during a batch; automation handles feed and both products through their marked hatches.

Each 160-tick batch at 24 JE/t consumes four stock units (three rubber for a hose). It produces eight sheets, six insulation pieces, three films or profiles, or one hose. Only films/profiles also return one matching clean offcut: at least as many as the Metal Press or Molding Press make from the same stock. Every required output drawer must have room before work starts. The existing Molding Press keeps its six molds and all prior recipes.

Power: lower front-left. Solid feed: front-right. Finished product: rear-right middle; extrusion offcuts: rear-right upper. Fluid feed: rear middle; fluid products: rear bottom. Pause, Cancel, progress, tank levels, energy, tool locks and upgrade slots use the shared factory screen. Recipes are fictional game quantities.

pages.title: Clean Polymer Reclaimer
text: Four same-grade clean offcuts return one stock unit for 120 ticks at 32 JE/t. Three unused LDPE films or PVC profiles also return one matching stock. There is no recipe for mixed trash, other grades, placed blocks or assembled machinery. Recycling pays power and loses material every cycle.

Film wraps cable insulation and cushions machine housings. PVC profiles brace housings and assemble existing colored-plastic blocks. Sheets, insulation and hoses use all their existing recipes. Look up exact construction uses in JEI.

Power: lower front-left. Solid feed: front-right. Finished product: rear-right middle; extrusion offcuts: rear-right upper. Fluid feed: rear middle; fluid products: rear bottom. Pause, Cancel, progress, tank levels, energy, tool locks and upgrade slots use the shared factory screen. Recipes are fictional game quantities.

pages.title: Acid Concentrator
text: Optional specialist model: existing machines, recipes, inventories and production remain supported. For a new factory, build the Concentrator, which also runs this machine's processes. This specialist stays craftable for existing layouts but is omitted from the main creative machinery list.

Separate 1000 mB ordinary sulfuric acid into 750 mB concentrate and 250 mB recovered water. Both outlets must fit. Reuse the existing starter acid factory; this is paid concentration, not a second free acid source.

Shared factory controls: Pause, Cancel, progress, energy, tanks and upgrades. Power at lower front-left; solid feed front-right and product rear-right; fluid feeds rear-middle and products rear-bottom. Processing is server-authoritative; no fluid is silently vented. Consult JEI for exact quantities and the encyclopedia for the connected route.

pages.title: Chemical Dissolution Chamber
text: Mine fluorite in snowy regions, including occasional exposed high mountain veins. The Mineral Conditioning Station washes one fluorite with 250 mB water into concentrate. Concentrate plus 750 mB concentrated sulfuric acid yields 500 mB hydrogen fluoride gas and one calcium sulfate. The washed-out water is consumed; these are game units, not chemical instructions.

Optional residue recovery: two calcium sulfate + 250 mB water in the Conditioner yields one Prepared Gypsum Binder, paying 160 ticks at 48 JE/t with a material loss. One binder + two sand + gravel crafts two white concrete powder as game construction filler. The chamber is ceramic-lined starter equipment and needs no PTFE. Retain the gas in tanks or cylinders; this machine has no gas vent.

Shared factory controls: Pause, Cancel, progress, energy, tanks and upgrades. Power at lower front-left; solid feed front-right and product rear-right; fluid feeds rear-middle and products rear-bottom. Processing is server-authoritative; no fluid is silently vented. Consult JEI for exact quantities and the encyclopedia for the connected route.
Also dissolves Ground Phosphate with ordinary sulfuric acid into slurry. Use the recipe picker; empty old fluid from the shared process outlet before switching from HF.

pages.title: Fluorocarbon Reactor
text: 500 mB methane + 1500 mB chlorine -> 500 mB chloroform + 1500 mB hydrogen chloride. Then 500 mB chloroform + 1000 mB hydrogen fluoride -> 500 mB chlorodifluoromethane + 1000 mB hydrogen chloride. Empty incompatible feeds/products before changing jobs; reserve room for every output.

Recovered hydrogen chloride goes to the existing Chemical Reactor absorption recipe. Methane can come from the biogas chain; chlorine comes from electrolysis or the magnesium line. No elemental fluorine is required for this route.

Shared factory controls: Pause, Cancel, progress, energy, tanks and upgrades. Power at lower front-left; solid feed front-right and product rear-right; fluid feeds rear-middle and products rear-bottom. Processing is server-authoritative; no fluid is silently vented. Consult JEI for exact quantities and the encyclopedia for the connected route.

pages.title: Fluoromonomer Cracker
text: 1000 mB chlorodifluoromethane -> 500 mB tetrafluoroethylene (TFE) + 500 mB hydrogen chloride. Work and heat are paid by JE. Feed 1000 mB TFE to the Polymerization Kettle with its reusable PTFE Process Insert to make four PTFE powder.

Shared factory controls: Pause, Cancel, progress, energy, tanks and upgrades. Power at lower front-left; solid feed front-right and product rear-right; fluid feeds rear-middle and products rear-bottom. Processing is server-authoritative; no fluid is silently vented. Consult JEI for exact quantities and the encyclopedia for the connected route.

pages.title: PTFE Sintering Oven
text: Optional specialist model: existing machines, recipes, inventories and production remain supported. For a new factory, build the Industrial Oven, which also runs this machine's processes. This specialist stays craftable for existing layouts but is omitted from the main creative machinery list.

PTFE is shaped before sintering. Use the Molding Press gasket, fitting or panel mold with 1, 2 or 3 powder respectively to make one unsintered seal, fitting or liner. The oven finishes each blank for 240 ticks at 80 JE/t.

Alternative liner route: mix four powder with 250 mB lubricant in the Mineral Conditioner, yielding four paste charges. The Extruder sheet die consumes four charges for one liner blank plus one clean unsintered offcut. Four offcuts return one powder in the Reclaimer, paying energy and losing material. Finished PTFE parts are not melt-recycled or substituted for generic plastic.

Shared factory controls: Pause, Cancel, progress, energy, tanks and upgrades. Power at lower front-left; solid feed front-right and product rear-right; fluid feeds rear-middle and products rear-bottom. Processing is server-authoritative; no fluid is silently vented. Consult JEI for exact quantities and the encyclopedia for the connected route.

pages.title: Lined Fluorochemical Reactor
text: Build with one finished PTFE seal, fitting and liner, two titanium ingots, two motors, a basic circuit and machine casing. This upgrade runs the same two fluorocarbon recipes in two independent lanes with 8000 mB tanks and 90% energy per lane, rounded up each tick. The starter reactor can produce every input to this upgrade.

Shared factory controls: Pause, Cancel, progress, energy, tanks and upgrades. Power at lower front-left; solid feed front-right and product rear-right; fluid feeds rear-middle and products rear-bottom. Processing is server-authoritative; no fluid is silently vented. Consult JEI for exact quantities and the encyclopedia for the connected route.

pages.title: Precision Finishing Station
text: Three blocks wide, deep and tall. One shared station grinds ceramic blanks and steel shafts, and polishes optical glass. Build it with ordinary steel, motors and a basic circuit; no precision output is needed to start.

Fit a Diamond Abrasive Head for insulators, alumina plates, bearing balls, zirconia inserts or shafts; fit a Felt Polishing Head for lenses. Both heads are reusable, manually installed tools. Their recipes use earlier supplies, not this station. They are never consumed by a batch.

Each job takes one blank and 125 mB water, runs for 200 ticks at 48 JE/t before upgrades, and returns all 125 mB to its separate outlet. Both the product drawer and water outlet must fit. Pipe the return into the feed to reuse coolant; a full outlet pauses production rather than destroying it.

Front lower left: power. Front right: blank input. Rear left, middle height: water inlet; directly below: returned water. Rear right: finished part. The visible splash tray, drain and coolant line serve those ports.

Use Recipes to preview costs and required tools, then Lock recipe. Alumina blanks have two jobs: plates or bearing balls. Automatic defaults to the alphabetically first compatible job, so lock the product before automating. A running batch keeps its reserved inputs when you change the next job.
Finish an assembled Stainless Valve with the Felt Polishing Head: 240 ticks at 48 JE/t, returning the same 125 mB cooling water. Its alternate vessel recipes feed existing chemical equipment.

pages.title: Wafer Wet-processing Bench
text: One shared 3 x 3 x 3 bench cleans, coats, develops and etches prepared wafers. The separate existing Lithography Station exposes the coated wafer between coating and developing. Use Recipes and Lock recipe to select a stage. Empty unused input tanks when changing jobs.

Front lower-left power; front-right wafer drawer; rear-left reagent and rear-middle rinse at middle height; rear-left low waste outlet; rear-right finished wafer drawer. All fluid services connect to the contained wash tray and sump. There are no unused decorative pipe ends.

Every wet job reserves space for its spent mixture before starting. Store and transport this mixture in existing tanks; recovery belongs to package 6. No automatic vent, free drain or recovery loop is introduced.

pages.title: Four shared process machines
text: Build a Concentrator for seawater or acid; a Gas Scrubber for synthesis gas, biogas or fermentation gas; a Filter Press for aluminate or digestate; and an Industrial Oven for drying, calcination or PTFE sintering. Each handles multiple resources without a separate named machine for every output.

The five older specialist designs stay craftable and continue working in existing factories. The four recommended machines also keep their original saved block IDs, inventories and ports. The Oven gains one connected solution inlet on its lower rear face.

Open Recipes to search and preview inputs, outputs and costs. Lock recipe chooses the only job new batches may start; Automatic restores input-driven selection. Saved locks also filter automated inputs. Drain incompatible input AND output fluids and clear other feed items when changing jobs; running batches finish unchanged.

pages.title: From Sand to Silicon
text: The electronics tier turns silicon into chips. It has the cyan look: dark casings, cyan glass and screens, violet conduits.
Pull a silicon boule from 4 silicon and a phosphate in the arc furnace, then saw it into 8 silicon wafers in the sawmill.

pages.title: Lithography Station
text: Three wide, two tall and two deep: a cleanroom and an operator's desk with a monitor bank. A silicon wafer, two copper wire and 100 mB of sulfuric acid make four microchips, every 10 seconds at 192 JE/t. Pipe the acid into its tank.
Uses 192 JE/t while working. Holds 60,000 JE.

pages.title: Processors
text: Four microchips, an advanced circuit and a gold ingot make a processor in the circuit assembler: the third circuit tier.

pages.title: Network Terminal
text: A beige retro computer. Cable it into a power network and right-click it: it shows the network's cables, the rate its slowest cable sets, how many devices it reaches and the energy they hold. It uses no power.

pages.title: Control Networks
text: Data cable (optical fibre in a plastic sheath) joins sensors, relays and a logic controller. It carries no power. Channels are the sixteen dye colours: use a dye on a sensor or relay to set its channel.

A sensor goes on a tank, battery, machine or chest and reads how full it is: energy first, then fluids, then items. It gives a redstone signal like a comparator's and reports the exact percentage on its channel. Right-click it to see the reading.
A relay gives a full redstone signal on every side while the controller has its channel on. Set a machine beside it to a redstone mode and the controller runs the machine.

pages.title: Logic Controller
text: Runs your factory by rules. Join sensors and relays to it with data cable, then right-click it: each of its eight rules reads "IF channel below or above N% THEN channel ON or OFF". Every second it averages each channel's sensors and works through the rules in order, a later rule overriding an earlier one; a channel no rule switches this time keeps its state, so two rules (off above 90%, on below 50%) leave a dead band. The strip along the bottom shows every channel's reading.

pages.title: The Control Room
text: Six control monitor panels in a wall, three wide and two tall, all facing the same way, form one screen. Run a data cable from any panel to a logic controller and it shows every channel: its colour, reading, a bar, a two-minute graph and whether the controller has it on.
An alarm klaxon is switched like a relay: while its channel is on it lights up and sounds.

A control remote flips one channel by hand. Use it on a logic controller to bind it, sneak and use it to pick the channel, and use it to switch. The controller's rules may switch the channel back when their condition next holds. It works within 256 blocks of the controller.

pages.title: Rocket Fuel
text: Rockets burn solid propellant: ammonium perchlorate (the oxidizer), aluminum and a rubber binder.

Ammonium perchlorate: a salt and 250 mB of ammonia in the chemical reactor make two. Iodine: eight dried kelp and 100 mB of sulfuric acid make one; with silver dust it makes silver iodide, which seeds clouds.

pages.title: Rocket Workshop
text: Builds rockets from up to three ingredients in any slots, like the circuit assembler: solid propellant from ammonium perchlorate, aluminum and rubber; casings, nozzles and guidance units; motors; and the rockets themselves.
Uses 48 JE/t while working. Holds 20,000 JE.

pages.title: Rockets
text: A rocket motor is a casing, a nozzle and two solid propellant. Fire any rocket with right-click under open sky; it rises like a firework and does its work at the top.

Survey rocket (motor, guidance unit, sensor): surveys ores and oil under 7x7 chunks. Cloud-seeding rocket (motor, two silver iodide): five minutes of rain. Clear-sky rocket (motor, two guncotton): five minutes of clear sky. Weather rockets share a two-minute cooldown.

Signal flares (four from propellant, paper and red dye) burst red and tell players within 512 blocks where they went up. Illumination flares (with glowstone) make hostile mobs within 48 blocks glow for 30 seconds.

pages.title: Rocket Post
text: A rocket pad sends its cargo to another pad up to 4096 blocks away in the same dimension. Sneak and use a flight plan on the pad to deliver to, then put the plan, a delivery rocket (motor, casing, guidance unit) and up to nine stacks of cargo in the sending pad.
Press Launch, or give the pad a redstone pulse. It needs open sky. The flight takes three seconds plus a second for every 80 blocks; the cargo lands in the target pad's slots.
If nobody is near the target, the rocket waits and lands as soon as that area is loaded again. Hoppers load a pad from the top and sides and unload it from the bottom.

pages.title: Ziplines
text: Place two zipline anchors up to 96 blocks apart with nothing solid between them. Stand within 4 blocks of one and use a line-throwing rocket while looking at the other: it strings a steel line.
Use either anchor with an empty hand to ride the line to the other end, hanging below it. A steeper drop is faster. Sneak to let go early (you fall from there).
Breaking either anchor takes the line down. Each anchor holds one line.

pages.title: Rocket Launcher
text: The rocket launcher fires a rocket from your inventory (the other hand first), straight and fast. One shot every two seconds.
High-explosive rockets (four from two solid propellant, two guncotton and a rocket casing in the rocket workshop) burst hard where they hit: twelve hearts at the centre, falling off over 5 blocks.
Homing rockets (with a guidance unit instead of the casing) lock on to the hostile mob nearest your crosshair within 48 blocks, if you can see it, and steer into it. Their blast is smaller.
Like grenades, rockets hurt living things only: they never break, move or burn a block.

pages.title: Liquid Fuels
text: RP-1 kerosene: hydrocrack heavy fuel oil with hydrogen (in the water tank) over the catalyst in the catalytic cracker. A bucket and 200 mB of hydrogen give 800 mB of kerosene, drawn off with the naphtha. It is jet fuel too: 448 JE/mB in the gas turbine, 480 in the advanced engine.
Liquid oxygen: the cryogenic liquefier condenses a bucket of oxygen into 250 mB.

Fill a rocket casing with a bucket of each in the chemical reactor to make a kerosene tank and a liquid oxygen tank. With two nozzles they make three rocket motors in the rocket workshop, with no solid propellant.

pages.title: Booster Rails
text: A booster rail is a straight rail with rocket thrusters. Power it with redstone like a powered rail; unpowered it is an ordinary rail and does not brake.
Load it with solid propellant (use it on the rail, or feed it from a hopper): each gives 8 boosts, up to 64 held.

A cart that rolls on to a powered, loaded booster rail (or stands on it) is kicked to full speed and held there for 10 seconds, up slopes too, trailing flame. A cart standing still goes uphill, or away from a block at one end.

pages.title: Machine Sides
text: Every processing machine's screen has six face buttons: front, back, left, right, top and bottom.
Click one to cycle: In (blue), Out (orange), Both (green) or Off (gray).
Eject makes the machine push its results out of its Out faces by itself.
The R button sets how it reacts to redstone: always run, run with a signal, or run without one.

pages.title: Brass Item Pipe
text: Joins inventories into a network. Items go to matching sorters first, then take turns between the other inventories.

pages.title: Pneumatic Extractor
text: Pulls 16 items every 8 ticks from what it faces and pushes them out of its other sides. A redstone signal pauses it.

pages.title: High-Pressure Extractor
text: A steel extractor: 32 items every 4 ticks, four times the brass one.

pages.title: Item Sorter
text: Takes only the items in its 9-slot filter, and puts them into the inventory it faces.

pages.title: Conveyor
text: Carries items the way you faced when placing it, 2.5 blocks a second, while rotation drives it. A shaft, gearbox or motor on any side drives every conveyor joined to it, for 1 KE per conveyor per tick. Pipes, hoppers and machines load it, and so do items dropped on it; at the end items go into the conveyor or inventory ahead, or onto the ground. It carries you too; sneak to stand still.

pages.title: Conveyor Splitter
text: A conveyor that sends items left, straight on and right in turn, skipping any way that is blocked.

pages.title: Conveyor Slope
text: Carries items one block up, onto the top of the block in front, or down from a conveyor one block higher behind it. Use it with an empty hand to switch between up and down. It joins and runs with the conveyors around it.

pages.title: Brass Wrench
text: Right-click turns a machine. Sneak and right-click to pick a Jugcraft block up, with everything inside.

pages.title: Item Crate
text: Holds 32 stacks of one item. Right-click with an item to put it in, with an empty hand to take a stack out (sneak to just look). Works with pipes, hoppers and comparators.

pages.title: Capacitor Bank
text: A 2x2 bank of Leyden jars: 4,000,000 JE. It charges from any side and gives power out of the sockets on its front, 4,096 JE/t.
Holds 4,000,000 JE; 4096 JE/t in and out.

pages.title: Steel Tank
text: A 2x2 riveted tank: 128 buckets of one fluid. Buckets, pumps and pipes fill and empty it; right-click with an empty hand to read it.
Needs no power.

pages.title: Gas Holder
text: A 3x3x3 sphere on legs: 1,024 buckets of one gas, and nothing but gases (liquids go in the steel tank). Pumps and pipes fill and empty it from any face; right-click with an empty hand to read it. Comparators read how full it is.
Needs no power.

pages.title: Water Wheel
text: Two blocks tall. The wheel on its right side turns in flowing water: 8 JE/t for each of its two blocks with flowing water beside it, 12 if the water is falling. Still water does not turn it.
Makes up to 24 JE/t. Holds 8,000 JE.

pages.title: Cobblestone Generator
text: Makes one cobblestone a second while water and lava touch it, on any sides. Neither is used up. Speed upgrades make it faster.
Uses 4 JE/t while working. Holds 4,000 JE.

pages.title: Tree Farm
text: Grows a sapling into six logs in 20 seconds and gives the sapling back, sometimes with an apple, cocoa beans or other extras. Feed the sapling back in with eject and a pipe for endless wood.
Uses 16 JE/t while working. Holds 10,000 JE.

pages.title: Crop Harvester
text: Two blocks tall. Harvests the ripe crops in the 9x9 field in front of it, starting the block in front: one crop a second at 24 JE/t. It keeps the drops and plants one of the seeds again, and waits when its three result slots are full. Crops on farmland sit at its own height.
Uses 24 JE/t while working. Holds 20,000 JE.

pages.title: Hydroponic Bay
text: Grows a seed or cutting in nutrient solution under grow lights: no soil, sunlight or farmland, so it works underground, in the Nether or the End. A harvest every 30 seconds uses 100 mB of solution (a fertilizer in a bucket of water, in the chemical reactor) and gives the seed back.
Uses 12 JE/t while working. Holds 20,000 JE.

pages.title: Sprinkler
text: Pipe water in (or use a water bucket) and it sprays the crops within 4 blocks, at its height and one below: every 5 seconds it uses 50 mB and gives each growing crop an extra growth tick. Load up to 16 fertilizer (by hand or hopper) and every 30 seconds it spreads one over the 5x5 crops around it.

pages.title: Cotton
text: Sift coarse dirt in the sieve: now and then it turns up cotton seeds (and wheat seeds).
Plant them on farmland like wheat. A ripe plant gives one to three cotton and more seeds; the harvester, sprinkler and fertilizer all work on it.
One cotton spins into one string.

pages.title: Speed Upgrade
text: In a machine's upgrade slot: each card makes it faster but uses more energy per item. Four cards: 3x as fast for twice the energy.

pages.title: Efficiency Upgrade
text: In a machine's upgrade slot: each card cuts energy use by a fifth. Four cards: 41% of the energy.

pages.title: Automation Upgrade
text: Enables saved recipe priorities and output stock targets in supported machines. Open Recipes to configure up to eight rules. Removing the card suspends the rules without deleting them.

pages.title: Comparators
text: A comparator next to a generator or battery shows how full it is.
Next to a processing machine, it shows how full its slots are, like a chest.

pages.title: Ceramics: powder to finished part
text: Pulverize clay balls into clay powder. Mix four powder, two quartz and one borax into four Porcelain Powder Blends. The Mineral Conditioner prepares each blend with 125 mB water. The existing Metal Press shapes the charge; the shared Industrial Oven fires it. Finish each fired blank into two porcelain insulators.

Alumina from the existing bauxite line follows the same conditioning, pressing and firing route. Finish one blank into an Alumina Plate or one set of Ceramic Bearing Balls. Lock the desired recipe; there is no separate ceramic press or kiln to build.

Before ceramics, the original terracotta insulator, motor and upgrade recipes still work. Ordinary clay bricks still start steel and chemistry. Ceramics are an optional productive specialty, not a retroactive gate.

pages.title: Precision parts and their uses
text: Two steel plates hand-assemble two shaft blanks. Finish them with the abrasive head. A shaft, a steel plate and a set of ceramic balls assemble a Precision Bearing. Bearings and shafts make two motors per advanced assembly, or a Speed Upgrade with less gear-making.

Finished Alumina Plates provide the insulating body of an alternate Efficiency Upgrade. Porcelain insulators make existing placed Ceramic Insulators and an alternate Copper Cable recipe. These are extra recipes: old recipes and saved equipment stay available.

Two borosilicate glass make two Optical Blanks. The Felt Polishing Head finishes each into a lens; two lenses, a brass plate and a compass make the existing Range Finder. Lenses also make spyglasses. Advanced wafer equipment will use this same finishing specialty in a later package.

pages.title: Specialist zirconia tooling
text: The Conditioner recovers one trace Zircon Concentrate from 16 sand and 1000 mB water. Two concentrate plus 500 mB lye make one precursor; calcine it in the Industrial Oven for zirconia powder. This expensive, deterministic starter route works in existing worlds without new chunks. Regional Zircon-rich Mineral Sand is the efficient route: two sand and 500 mB water produce one concentrate.

Condition, press and fire zirconia like alumina, then finish one fired blank into two cutting inserts. An insert, steel plate and iron ingot craft a reusable polymer mold or extrusion die in a selected pattern. The original all-metal tool recipes remain available.

Inputs and costs are simplified game balance. Consumed preparation liquids are spent; only the Finisher returns its cooling water. There is no recycling recipe that turns finished components back into more feedstock.

pages.title: Precision Finishing Station
text: Three blocks wide, deep and tall. One shared station grinds ceramic blanks and steel shafts, and polishes optical glass. Build it with ordinary steel, motors and a basic circuit; no precision output is needed to start.

Fit a Diamond Abrasive Head for insulators, alumina plates, bearing balls, zirconia inserts or shafts; fit a Felt Polishing Head for lenses. Both heads are reusable, manually installed tools. Their recipes use earlier supplies, not this station. They are never consumed by a batch.

Each job takes one blank and 125 mB water, runs for 200 ticks at 48 JE/t before upgrades, and returns all 125 mB to its separate outlet. Both the product drawer and water outlet must fit. Pipe the return into the feed to reuse coolant; a full outlet pauses production rather than destroying it.

Front lower left: power. Front right: blank input. Rear left, middle height: water inlet; directly below: returned water. Rear right: finished part. The visible splash tray, drain and coolant line serve those ports.

Use Recipes to preview costs and required tools, then Lock recipe. Alumina blanks have two jobs: plates or bearing balls. Automatic defaults to the alphabetically first compatible job, so lock the product before automating. A running batch keeps its reserved inputs when you change the next job.
Finish an assembled Stainless Valve with the Felt Polishing Head: 240 ticks at 48 JE/t, returning the same 125 mB cooling water. Its alternate vessel recipes feed existing chemical equipment.

pages.title: Regional chromite to stainless steel
text: Find dark chromite in new chunks beneath windswept hills, windswept forest, stony peaks, stony shores, Shield and Highland. Its host province follows the surface biome even when you enter a cave. Occasional exposed outcrops mark a local source. Mine with an iron pickaxe or better, or trade with another player. Old chunks are not rewritten.

Condition two chromite with 250 mB water into two concentrate, then reduce both with one Coke in the Arc Furnace into two Ferrochromium Ingots. Preparation water is spent, not free recoverable coolant. Ferrochromium is iron/chromium alloying stock, not pure chromium.

The existing Alloy Smelter takes six Steel Ingots, two Ferrochromium Ingots and one Nickel Ingot to make nine Stainless Steel Ingots in 400 ticks. Nickel comes from its existing independent ore route. The existing Metal Press makes one plate per ingot. No stainless equipment is required to make the first batch.
These convenient game ratios conserve input metal units; they do not represent a certified real-world grade. There is no reverse recipe separating alloys into their ingredients.

pages.title: Chemical vessels and precision valves
text: Press one Stainless Steel Plate into two pipe fittings. Four plates and two finished Alumina Plates craft one Ceramic-lined Stainless Vessel. One fitting, a gasket and a Precision Shaft assemble an unfinished valve; finish it using the Felt Polishing Head, 125 mB returned cooling water, 240 ticks and 48 JE/t.

Use these parts in alternate Steel Fluid Pipe, Steel Tank, Bulk Chemical Reactor and Lined Fluorochemical Reactor recipes. The lined reactor still needs its PTFE liner, seal and fitting. Stainless substitutes for selected construction parts; it does not bypass the first PTFE production route.

The outputs are the existing machines and transport blocks, with their existing capacities, models and behavior. Stainless recipes offer different material bills; they do not secretly add corrosion resistance, extra throughput or storage. Every older recipe stays available.

pages.title: Lightweight structural alloy
text: Seven Aluminum Ingots and one Magnesium Ingot make eight Aluminum-Magnesium Alloy Ingots in the Alloy Smelter, 240 ticks. Use the existing bauxite and coastal-seawater magnesium routes. This approximate whole-ingot game batch conserves all eight metal units.

Press each ingot to a plate and each plate to one formed panel. Four alloy plates and one Precision Shaft craft two lightweight frames. Panels feed Rocket Workshop casings; frames support an alternate Zeppelin recipe. Frames and panels also provide an alternate Howitzer Walker assembly, keeping its Diesel Walker core, dispenser and pistons.

These are manufacturing alternatives, not different vehicle stats or hidden weight bonuses. Existing vehicle construction and worlds remain supported. Titanium alloys and new armor/tool tiers remain separate future work.

pages.title: Lead-acid workshop storage
text: An early bank stores 2,000,000 JE and transfers up to 1,024 JE/t in each direction. It starts empty. Existing Battery Boxes and Capacitor Banks remain unchanged and all original lithium recipes remain available.

Existing raw lead represents galena feed. Condition two raw lead with 250 mB water, then reduce two concentrate with one Coke in the Arc Furnace into two Lead Ingots. Old lead refining still works. Press lead plates to grids; oxidize one grid with 250 mB oxygen in the Bulk Chemical Reactor.

Press one Plastic Sheet into four separators. Craft a lead grid, an oxide electrode and a separator into a dry cell, then fill it with 250 mB sulfuric acid in the Bulk Chemical Reactor. Craft four filled cells with steel plates, copper wire and a basic circuit into a bank. Acid is incorporated once; there is no cycle-aging upkeep.

pages.title: Expanded lithium cells
text: Fire Spodumene in the Industrial Oven, then condition two activated mineral with 500 mB sulfuric acid for two Lithium Carbonate. Existing lepidolite and lithium recipes remain available.

In the Bulk Chemical Reactor prepare Lithium Fluoride from carbonate and HF, and a fluorophosphate precursor from phosphate and HF. Combine both in the two-input Chemical Reactor to LiPF6 salt. Separately make Dry Carbonate Solvent Charges from bioethanol and carbon dioxide in the Bulk Reactor. One salt plus two solvent charges in the Chemical Reactor yields two formulated electrolyte charges. These sealed process doses are abstract game batches, not buckets or real laboratory instructions.

Craft lithium carbonate, iron and phosphate into a Cathode Mix, then process it in the Bulk Reactor for two Lithium Iron Phosphate Cathodes. Press Coke to Carbon Anodes and plastic sheets to separators. Craft cathode, anode, separator and aluminum plate into a dry cell assembly, then fill it with one electrolyte charge in the Circuit Assembler. It produces the existing Lithium Cell, for the existing 32,000,000 JE / 16,384 JE/t bank.

pages.title: Paired flow modules and mineral electrolyte
text: Existing vanadium-bearing iron concentrate and its roasted Vanadium Oxide now feed Vanadyl Sulfate with Coke and sulfuric acid in the two-input Chemical Reactor; the existing Pentoxide is an alternative. Formulate one sulfate charge with 500 mB acid and 500 mB water in the Bulk Reactor into 1,000 mB of the existing Vanadium Electrolyte. Refinery-residue electrolyte stays available.

A Flow Battery still begins with two internal sides totaling 64 buckets / 64,000,000 JE. Place up to four paired tank modules in a straight row immediately behind the middle bottom block, facing the same way as the controller. Each paired module adds 64 buckets, equally split between both sides. Maximum: 320 buckets / 320,000,000 JE. Fill through the controller; modules never own a second copy of fluid or energy.

Place one Cell-stack Module directly above the middle front top block to raise both input and output from 8,192 to 16,384 JE/t. Capacity and rate are separate upgrades. Attached joints align with the module manifolds; modules need no standalone cables or fluid pipes.

Removing or unloading required tank modules suspends transfers when stored electrolyte exceeds connected capacity, preserving fluid and charge until the modules return. Breaking the controller keeps electrolyte but loses charge, as before. Detached modules are empty. No electrolyte is generated or consumed by charging.

pages.title: Local battery controls
text: Open any battery to select Automatic, Charge only, Discharge only or Off. Reserve changes in 10% steps; discharge stops at that reserve and resumes after charging five percentage points above it. At 0% reserve the original automatic behavior remains.

Charge priority chooses Low, Normal or High on the local cable network; higher priority is offered power first, with unused power falling through to the next group. This does not schedule generators or remotely command other grids. Output limit cycles 100%, 50% and 25%. Tick budgets are shared across every face and part.

All controls are server-authoritative, saved with the placed bank, and shown on its screen. Batteries start empty; energy transfer remains lossless for compatibility, subject to finite storage, cable limits, mode, reserve and rate. No charging cycles create energy.

pages.title: One liquefier, three cooling stages
text: Keep the existing oxygen route: 1000 mB oxygen becomes 250 mB Liquid Oxygen in 80 ticks at base 96 JE/t. No cooling module is needed. Electrolysis and air separation remain the gas supplies.

Install a retained Methane Cooling Module in the Cryogenic Liquefier tool slot for 1000 mB methane to 250 mB liquid methane, 160 ticks at base 96 JE/t. Existing cleaned biogas and methanation supply methane. The advanced Hydrogen Cooling Module also supports methane.

The advanced module enables 1000 mB hydrogen to 250 mB liquid hydrogen, 320 ticks at base 96 JE/t. It builds on the methane module, precision bearings, ceramic insulation and an advanced chip. Both modules are manual tooling, never consumed or exposed to hoppers.

Clear incompatible fluid before changing recipes. Changing a module discards cooling progress, never fluid. Missing tooling pauses production. These compact machines use their existing tank controls; the formed chemistry machines retain their recipe picker, previews and locks.

pages.title: Insulated storage and gas recovery
text: Craft Cryogenic Insulation from PTFE liners, an alumina plate and a porcelain insulator. The Insulated Fluid Tank holds 32 buckets; the Vacuum-insulated Fluid Tank holds 64. Silver jackets, olive collars and six centered service faces match the factory palette.

Both use the existing fluid pipes, pumps, tank groups and gauge. Connected compatible tanks share capacity. Break and replace a tank to retain its contents. Craft new tanks from raw parts, never from a filled tank. Existing tanks and cylinders retain their existing fluid compatibility.
No boil-off timer, hidden pressure system or world damage is introduced. Insulated storage is an optional compact capacity upgrade; old fuel factories keep working.

The Chemical Distillation Station vaporizes 250 mB LOX, liquid methane or liquid hydrogen into 1000 mB of the matching gas, using 160 ticks at base 32 JE/t. Lock the desired recipe and empty the first output before switching gases. The cooling/vaporization loop returns only its starting gas and consumes power.

pages.title: Storable propellants and residue
text: These are fictional game recipes. In the Bulk Chemical Reactor, one redstone, 500 mB ammonia and 250 mB nitrogen produce 250 mB hydrazine and one Propellant Process Residue. The N2O4 job uses one redstone and 500 mB nitric acid for 250 mB N2O4 and one residue.
Both jobs use base 96 JE/t; hydrazine takes 400 ticks and N2O4 takes 320. The process outlet and solid output must both have room. Existing ammonia, nitrogen and acid production supplies this branch.

Wash two residue with 500 mB water in the Mineral Conditioner to obtain 500 mB Process Recovery Concentrate. The existing clay stabilization and concrete-fill recipe then give it a construction use. Raw propellant residue is not fertilizer or fuel.

Hydrazine supplies the monopropellant thruster; N2O4 is only paired with hydrazine in the storable bipropellant assembly. MMH, orbital vehicles, destination progression and maneuvering simulation remain future work.

pages.title: Loaded motors for rockets you already have
text: The compact Chemical Reactor seals 1000 mB of liquid methane, liquid hydrogen, hydrazine or N2O4 into one Rocket Casing. These sealed items are manufacturing ingredients, not refillable fluid containers. Existing kerosene and LOX tank recipes remain available.

Rocket Workshop: one methane tank, one LOX tank and two nozzles yield three loaded Methalox Motors. Replace methane with hydrogen to yield four Hydrolox Motors. One hydrazine tank, one N2O4 tank and two nozzles yield three Storable Bipropellant Motors.

One hydrazine tank, one nozzle and one Porcelain Insulator make one Hydrazine Thruster. All four loaded motor options substitute for the ordinary motor in Survey, Cloud-seeding, Clear-sky, Delivery and Line Rocket recipes. Mixing incompatible propellant tank pairs never matches a recipe.

Payload behavior and range stay the same: the choice changes factory inputs and batch yield. Solid motors and RP-1/LOX remain valid. A loaded motor is consumed when assembling a rocket, including its propellant and casing; it is not an empty engine or a planet-launch unlock.

pages.title: Independent cobalt supply
text: Find Cobaltite beneath windswept hills, windswept forest, stony peaks, Shield or Highland in newly generated Overworld chunks, from Y -48 to 32. Occasional surface outcrops identify the host province. Mine with iron or better, survey or trade; existing terrain is never rewritten. Nickel mining stays separate.

Wash two Cobaltite with 500 mB water in the Mineral Conditioner into two Cobalt Concentrate and 500 mB Spent Mineral Wash. The existing wash-settling route accepts that waste. The Arc Furnace reduces two concentrate with one Coke into two Cobalt Ingots.

Craft two cobalt ingots over three fired vanilla bricks into one Cobalt-Ceramic Catalyst Bed. Install it in the Chemical Infuser tool socket. It is retained without wear and cannot be removed during a running batch. No synthetic fuel is required to make the first bed. Nickel methanation and vanadium contact beds keep their separate jobs.

pages.title: Clean gases to synthetic crude
text: Existing Coal Gasifiers process coal, charcoal or Coke and water into dirty synthesis gas. The existing Gas Scrubber cleans it with wash water, giving separate carbon monoxide, hydrogen and mixed gas-cleaning residue. Keep the existing residue stabilization route; dirty gas cannot enter synthesis directly.

Use existing electrolysis for extra hydrogen. Alternatively the Chemical Infuser, with the cobalt bed, converts 250 mB carbon monoxide and 500 mB water into 250 mB hydrogen (first outlet) and 250 mB CO2 (second). This trades carbon feed and power for hydrogen, not free fuel. The CO2 can use existing storage and methanation.

With the cobalt bed, infuse 500 mB clean CO and 1000 mB hydrogen into 500 mB Synthetic Crude and 500 mB water, 400 ticks at base 128 JE/t. These are simplified game batches. Use Recipes and Lock recipe; clear old products before switching jobs. Product outlet is at the rear, with the second outlet below.

The existing Infuser Drain excess water option applies only to plain water. Switch it off to capture all synthesis water and stop when full. CO2 from gas balancing is never silently drained. Existing gas tanks/cylinders, fluid tanks and pipes carry the supplies and products.

pages.title: One refinery, standard finished fuels
text: Feed 500 mB Synthetic Crude into the existing Distillation Tower. Collect 50 mB Refinery Gas in outlet 0, 150 mB Naphtha in outlet 1, 250 mB Diesel in outlet 2 and 50 mB Heavy Fuel Oil in outlet 3. All four products need space; outlet 4 remains unused. The compact tower uses its existing processing controls.

Diesel is already usable in compatible engines and vehicles. Existing Catalytic Cracker recipes finish naphtha into gasoline and refinery gas, or crack heavy oil into lighter fractions. Existing vacuum distillation produces lubricant and asphalt binder; existing hydrocracking prepares rocket kerosene.

Finished products retain the same IDs, energy values and compatibility as oil-derived fuels. The crude mixture itself is not a registered generator fuel. Refinery gas also supplies existing polymer chemistry. Account for gasification, wash, hydrogen, synthesis and refining energy together before judging the line profitable.

pages.title: Recover process water, contain residues
text: Wafer jobs share one Spent Wafer Mixture, so recovery cannot assume that every batch contains recoverable acid, alcohol or metal. No purity upgrade or arbitrary reagent restoration is granted.

The Mineral Conditioner treats 1000 mB spent mixture with 250 mB lye and one Calcite block into 1000 mB Treated Process Water (outlet 0) plus 250 mB Process Recovery Concentrate (outlet 1). The Chemical Distillation Station processes that treated water into 750 mB water and another 250 mB concentrate.

Condition 1000 mB concentrate with one clay ball into four Stabilized Process Residue. Craft two residue, two sand and two gravel into four ordinary Gray Concrete Powder. This is fictional paid preparation for game construction, not a real waste-handling procedure. Raw concentrate has no fuel, fertilizer or food use.

Both recovery stages use 320 ticks at base 64 JE/t. No waste is silently deleted. Fill every required output and the job waits; use shared recipe previews, locks and stock targets. Earlier gas-cleaning, mineral-wash, digestate and gypsum routes remain useful.

pages.title: Phosphate into useful supplies
text: Pulverize one existing Phosphate into one Ground Phosphate. The Chemical Dissolution Chamber combines two ground phosphate and 1000 mB ordinary sulfuric acid into 1000 mB slurry. Its existing process outlet now serves either HF or slurry; empty it when changing recipes.

The shared Filter Press converts 1000 mB slurry into 750 mB Industrial Phosphoric Acid (first fluid outlet), 250 mB water (second) and two Gypsum-rich Residue (first item output). Nothing is vented: blocked byproducts stop production. Use the recipe picker, previews and persistent Lock recipe.

The Bulk Chemical Reactor combines one ground phosphate and 250 mB acid into two Wet Superphosphate. The shared Industrial Oven dries each into one Triple Superphosphate, returning 125 mB water. Recipes are abstract game batches, not real manufacturing instructions.

pages.title: Choose a fertilizer for your farm
text: Nitrogen Field Fertilizer gives four bone-meal applications to tagged grains, leaves and fibre crops; Triple Superphosphate gives four to tagged roots, legumes and fruiting crops. Either gives one application to other crops. Mixed-farm Fertilizer gives three to every eligible crop. Vanilla growth rules still decide the result; these are growth applications, not guaranteed harvests.

Use on a crop or ground to reach a 5 x 5 area, one block up or down. Tall plants count once. An item is only consumed if growth succeeds. Decorations and trees are excluded. The tooltip and use message identify the selected specialty.

The Conditioner makes four Organic Fertilizer Carriers from one Organic Compost and 250 mB water, or one carrier from two Digestate Fiber and 250 mB water. The compact Chemical Reactor blends one ammonium nitrate and one carrier into two Nitrogen Field Fertilizers. Craft one nitrogen fertilizer, one Triple Superphosphate and one carrier into two Mixed-farm Fertilizers.

Existing bone meal, ordinary fertilizer, ammonium nitrate and rich-soil compost routes stay available. Compost still offers passive soil improvement; the carrier route consumes the unplaced block instead. Crop groups live in fertilizer_nitrogen_crops and fertilizer_phosphate_crops block tags for datapack extensions.

pages.title: Sprinklers and hydroponics
text: Load one fertilizer type at a time into a sprinkler by hand, hopper or item pipe. It stores up to 16. New blends keep their crop-group effect when the existing water-powered fertilizer pulse runs. Ordinary Fertilizer keeps its previous effect; old saves retain their stored count.

Use an empty hand to read the loaded fertilizer type and count. Sneak-use with an empty hand retrieves the fertilizer and any stored buckets so you can change the load. Sprinklers do not bypass town protection for the new blends. No background crop scanning or chunk loading is added.

The Bulk Reactor dissolves one Mixed-farm Fertilizer with 1000 mB water into 1000 mB existing Nutrient Solution for hydroponics. This gives ordinary nutrient solution, without a hidden crop bonus. The earlier ordinary-fertilizer nutrient recipe remains useful.

pages.title: Gypsum and battery integration
text: Condition two Gypsum-rich Residue with 500 mB water into one Washed Gypsum and 500 mB Spent Mineral Wash. The Industrial Oven prepares one washed gypsum into one existing Gypsum Binder. Keep the wash for the existing settling/recovery route; raw residue cannot be placed as a building block.

Craft one binder with two sand into two Plaster blocks, or two binder, two paper and one Digestate Fiber into four Plasterboard blocks. Both have matching slabs and stairs. Existing calcium-sulfate binder and concrete recipes remain available.

The compact Chemical Reactor can also turn 250 mB Industrial Phosphoric Acid and 500 mB HF into one existing Fluorophosphate Precursor for the battery chain. The earlier direct phosphate route remains available. This industrial acid is not a food-grade cola ingredient.

pages.title: From silicon to a polished wafer
text: Existing silicon, wafer, microchip and circuit routes remain available. For the optional advanced line, condition four Silicon with 500 mB hydrochloric acid and 500 mB water into two High-purity Silicon and 1000 mB spent mixture. Water conditioning is internal; there is no new purified-water currency.

Pull four high-purity silicon with one Phosphate in the Arc Furnace into one boule. The Precision Finisher slices it into eight process wafers with a reusable Diamond Abrasive Head and 250 mB returned cooling water. Change to the reusable Felt Polishing Head to polish each wafer with 125 mB returned water.

pages.title: Wafer reagents and waste
text: The Mineral Conditioner purifies sulfuric acid. The Bulk Reactor combines oxygen and water into process feed; the powered Electrolytic Separator turns it into peroxide and returned water. This is its own paid process, separate from ordinary water electrolysis.

Abstract game recipes use Coke and bioethanol for Novolac Resin, Coke and nitric acid for DNQ Additive, and ammonium nitrate, bioethanol and lye for Developer Charges. Dissolve the charges with water in the Bulk Reactor; blend Novolac and DNQ with bioethanol in the compact Chemical Reactor for photoresist. These doses simplify industrial chemistry for gameplay.

The bench cleans with electronic-grade sulfuric acid and peroxide, coats with photoresist, develops exposed wafers with TMAH and water, then etches with HF and water. Each step outputs spent mixture. Store it for the later recovery chain; a full waste outlet stops work.

pages.title: Exposure and useful chips
text: Craft a General-chip Pattern Plate from earlier glass lenses, gold ingot and a basic circuit. Install it manually in the new upper pattern slot of the existing Lithography Station. It is retained without wear. The station exposes a coated wafer into an exposed wafer; old acid-etch microchip recipes do not need a plate.

After developing and etching, the Circuit Assembler bonds each etched wafer with two copper wire and one solder ingot into four General-purpose Advanced Chips. Assemble those with precision parts for two Speed Upgrades, ceramic insulation and wire for two Efficiency Upgrades, or a basic circuit and polymer housing for one Automation Card.

Speed and Efficiency keep their existing four-card caps and effects. Automation works in powered formed machines with upgrade slots; compact machines keep their existing controls. It never remotely operates another machine.

pages.title: Recipe priorities and stock targets
text: Install an Automation Card in a formed machine upgrade slot, open Recipes, select a job and use Priority or Stock. Up to eight jobs per machine may have non-default settings. Priority 0 is normal; 1, 2 and 3 run first when their inputs, tool and output room are available. Recipe Lock still restricts work to the locked job.

Stock limits count the first item output, or first fluid output for fluid-only recipes, inside this machine plus matching outputs already promised by running lanes. They do not count remote chests or tanks. A batch starts only if its entire matching output fits below the target. Exporting products makes room to resume.

Item targets cycle Off, 16, 32, 64; fluid targets Off, 250, 500, 1000, 2000 mB. Choose a target at least as large as one batch. Running batches finish unchanged when settings change. Removing the card disables its rules but preserves them for reinsertion and world reload. Reset both settings to release a rule slot.
